National and regional prevalence estimates were analyzed, with additional subanalyses by ethnicity, type, and severity.

Main outcome measures

Pooled estimates for the prevalence of CVD.

Results

The global prevalence of CVD was estimated at 2.59% (95% confidence interval [CI], 2.20-3.03; I2 = 99.37), with higher rates observed in male patients (4.38% [95% CI, 3.93%-4.88%]) compared with female patients (0.64% [95% CI, 0.46%-0.89%]). Among ancestries, individuals of European descent exhibited the highest prevalence (2.77% [95% CI, 2.10%-3.64%]), closely followed by those of African descent (2.69% [95% CI, 2.21%-3.28%]). Regionally, Oceania displayed the highest prevalence (4.37% [95% CI, 3.36%-5.68%]), followed by Africa (2.86% [95% CI, 2.36%-3.46%]). Across all CVD types and severities, male patients consistently showed higher prevalence rates than female patients. In terms of CVD types, the highest prevalence was observed for deutan in both sexes (male, 3.66% [95% CI, 3.02%-4.44%]; female, 0.46% [95% CI, 0.30%-0.69%]), followed by protan (male, 1.54% [95% CI, 1.30%-1.82%]; female, 0.30% [95% CI, 0.21%-0.43%]) and tritan (male, 0.67% [95% CI, 0.20%-2.22%]). Regarding severity, male patients showed the highest prevalence of dichromacy (1.59% [95% CI, 1.33%-1.90%]), followed by anomalous trichromacy (1.17% [95% CI, 0.89%-1.55%]) and monochromacy (0.36% [95% CI, 0.22%-0.61%]). For female patients, anomalous trichromacy showed the highest prevalence (0.38% [95% CI, 0.25%-0.56%]), followed by dichromacy (0.27% [95% CI, 0.19%-0.39%]) and monochromacy (0.10% [95% CI, 0.04%-0.21%]).

Conclusions

This study highlights that the prevalence of CVD varies significantly by region and ethnicity.

Financial disclosure(s)

The author(s) have no proprietary or commercial interest in any materials discussed in this article.

records.title: Effect of Intravenous Mannitol on Intraocular Pressure Changes in Vitrectomized and Non-Vitrectomized Eyes: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

content.title: Effect of Intravenous Mannitol on Intraocular Pressure Changes in Vitrectomized and Non-Vitrectomized Eyes: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

Intraocular pressure (IOP) control is paramount during ophthalmic surgeries to ensure successful outcomes and prevent complications. Intravenous mannitol has been explored for its ability to manage IOP fluctuations in both vitrectomized and non-vitrectomized eyes. This meta-analysis aimed to assess the efficacy of mannitol in controlling IOP across these patient groups.

Design

Systematic review and meta-analysis.

Methods

A literature search was conducted across PubMed, EMBASE, Scopus, and Web of Science from inception up to March 1, 2024, focusing on studies investigating mannitol's impact on IOP in vitrectomized and non-vitrectomized eyes. Randomized controlled trials, cohort studies, and case-control studies were included, while case reports and review articles were excluded. The primary outcome was the change in IOP following mannitol administration. Meta-analysis was performed using a random-effects model. R software (V 4.3) was used for statistical analysis.

Results

Our search included five studies of both vitrectomized (145 eyes) and non-vitrectomized eyes (91 eyes). The meta-analysis demonstrated significant IOP reductions following mannitol administration across multiple time points. Three studies were included at 30 min and 2 studies at all other time points in the analysis. In vitrectomized eyes, notable decreases were observed: at 30 min, the Ratio of Means (ROM) was 0.81 (95% CI: 0.53; 1.24), indicating a 19% reduction; at 60 min, the ROM of 0.833 (95% CI: 0.77; 0.89) showed a 16.7% reduction; at 90 min, the ROM of 0.757 (95% CI: 0.755; 0.758) corresponded to a 24.3% reduction; at 2 h, the ROM of 0.726 (95% CI: 0.642; 0.820) reflected a 27.4% reduction; at 3 h, the ROM of 0.692 (95% CI: 0.600; 0.797) resulted in a 30.8% reduction; and at 4 h, the ROM of 0.700 (95% CI: 0.363; 1.350) indicated a 30% reduction. No significant changes were observed on IOP with mannitol administration when comparing vitrectomized versus non- vitrectomized eyes.

Conclusion

Intravenous mannitol effectively reduces IOP in both vitrectomized and non-vitrectomized eyes, demonstrating its utility in the acute management of elevated IOP during and after ophthalmic surgeries. These findings support the integration of mannitol into perioperative care protocols. However, further research, particularly randomized controlled trials and studies with broader demographic representation, is needed to optimize mannitol's usage and fully understand its long-term safety and efficacy.

records.title: Drug Exposure As a Predictor in Diabetic Retinopathy Risk Prediction Models-A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

content.title: Drug Exposure As a Predictor in Diabetic Retinopathy Risk Prediction Models-A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To conduct a systematic review to assess drug exposure handling in diabetic retinopathy (DR) risk prediction models, a network-meta-analysis to identify drugs associated with DR and a meta-analysis to determine which drugs contributed to enhanced model performance.

Design

Systematic review and meta-analysis.

Methods

We included studies presenting DR models incorporating drug exposure as a predictor. We searched EMBASE, MEDLINE, and SCOPUS from inception to December 2023. We evaluated the quality of studies using the Prediction model Risk of Bias Assessment Tool and certainty using GRADE. We conducted network meta-analysis and meta-analysis to estimate the odds ratio (OR) and pooled C-statistic, respectively, and 95% confidence intervals (CI) (PROSPERO: CRD42022349764).

Results

Of 5,653 records identified, we included 28 studies of 678,837 type 1 or 2 diabetes participants, of which 38,579 (5.7%) had DR. A total of 19, 3, and 7 studies were at high, unclear, and low risk of bias, respectively. Drugs included in models as predictors were: insulin (n = 24), antihypertensives (n = 5), oral antidiabetics (n = 12), lipid-lowering drugs (n = 7), antiplatelets (n = 2). Drug exposure was modelled primarily as a categorical variable (n = 23 studies). Two studies handled drug exposure as time-varying covariates, and one as a time-dependent covariate. Insulin was associated with an increased risk of DR (OR = 2.50; 95% CI: 1.61-3.86). Models that included insulin (n = 9) had a higher pooled C-statistic (C-statistic = 0.84, CI: 0.80-0.88), compared to models (n = 9) that incorporated a combination of drugs alongside insulin (C-statistic = 0.79, CI: 0.74-0.84), as well as models (n = 3) not including insulin (C-statistic = 0.70, CI: 0.64-0.75). Limitations include the high risk of bias and significant heterogeneity in reviewed studies.

Conclusion

This is the first review assessing drug exposure handling in DR prediction models. Drug exposure was primarily modelled as a categorical variable, with insulin associated with improved model performance. However, due to suboptimal drug handling, associations between other drugs and model performance may have been overlooked. This review proposes the following for future DR prediction models: (1) evaluation of drug exposure as a variable, (2) use of time-varying methodologies, and (3) consideration of drug regimen details. Improving drug exposure handling could potentially unveil novel variables capable of significantly enhancing the predictive capability of prediction models.

records.title: NSAIDs and Corticosteroids for the Postoperative Management of Age-Related Cataract Surgery: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.

content.title: NSAIDs and Corticosteroids for the Postoperative Management of Age-Related Cataract Surgery: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the safety and efficacy of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) and corticosteroids in the postoperative management of cataract surgery for age-related cataract in adults.

Design

Meta-analysis.

Methods

Cochrane, Embase, PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science and CINAHL were searched for articles using the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) system. The review was registered prospectively with PROSPERO (CRD42022364733). Randomized controlled trials of patients undergoing age-related cataract surgery treated with corticosteroids, NSAIDs, or a combination were included.

Results

A total of 19 studies were included, with 3473 patients (3638 eyes) treated following cataract surgery with NSAIDs (n = 1479), corticosteroids (n = 1307), or a combination (n = 687). Combination treatment demonstrated favorable best-corrected visual acuity compared to corticosteroids 4 to 6 weeks postoperatively (MD = -0.01 logMAR, 95% CI: -0.02, -0.01, I2 = 0%). NSAIDs had more favorable flare values than corticosteroids on day 7 (MD = -9.17 photons/ms, 95% CI = -16.52, -1.82, I2 = 94%), day 14 (MD = -5.23 photons/ms, 95% CI = -8.35, -2.11, I2 = 94%), and 4 to 6 weeks (MD = -1.62 photons/ms, 95% CI = -3.03, -0.20, I2 = 93%) postoperatively. Furthermore, 4 to 8 weeks postoperatively, patients treated with NSAIDs showed lower central macular thickness (MD = -13.26 µm, 95% CI = -18.66, -7.86, I2 = 81%) compared to those treated with corticosteroids. NSAIDs and combination treatment were associated with a lower incidence of central macular edema (OR = 0.16, 95% CI = 0.07, 0.35, I2 = 61%; OR = 0.21, 95% CI = 0.10, 0.45, I2 = 31%) than corticosteroids 4 to 8 weeks postoperatively.

Conclusions

NSAIDs and combination treatments could be regarded as more effective and safer alternatives to corticosteroids alone in the postoperative management of cataract surgery. Further studies should be conducted to determine why this evidence has not been reflected in practice patterns, and to further compare the effectiveness of NSAIDs and combination treatments.

records.title: Minimally invasive glaucoma surgery in the surgical landscape of primary angle closure glaucoma: Current innovations and future trends.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Minimally invasive glaucoma surgery in the surgical landscape of primary angle closure glaucoma: Current innovations and future trends.
content.abstract: Primary angle-closure glaucoma (PACG) is a major cause of irreversible blindness worldwide, with the highest burden in Asia. Its pathogenesis involves the interplay of multiple mechanisms, including pupillary block, plateau iris configuration, lens-related crowding, and dynamic choroidal expansion. Traditional surgical management has relied on trabeculectomy, lens extraction, or transscleral cyclophotocoagulation, which often achieve substantial intraocular pressure (IOP) control but carry significant risks and require prolonged recovery. Minimally invasive glaucoma surgery (MIGS) expands treatment options for PACG once angle access is restored. It offers safer, earlier, and targeted interventions tailored to the underlying mechanisms. Techniques range from trabecular meshwork (TM) and Schlemm's canal-based procedures to subconjunctival stents and ciliary body approaches. Combined with lens extraction, these methods deepen the anterior chamber, release peripheral anterior synechiae, and restore physiological outflow, with clinical evidence showing 20-50% IOP reductions and reduced medication burden. This paper reviews anatomical, physiological, and clinical evidence for the use of MIGS in PACG, discussing how these procedures can complement, or in selected cases replace, invasive filtration surgery, potentially enabling earlier intervention while maintaining a favorable safety profile. Future advancements will hinge on device refinements for narrow-angle eyes, imaging-guided precision, biologic modulation, and strategies to enhance cost-effectiveness and accessibility, ultimately enabling individualized, mechanism-based treatment pathways.

records.title: Are Müller glial cells gatekeepers of neuroprotection and regeneration in age-related macular degeneration? Unraveling their roles in pathophysiology and therapeutic innovation.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Are Müller glial cells gatekeepers of neuroprotection and regeneration in age-related macular degeneration? Unraveling their roles in pathophysiology and therapeutic innovation.
content.abstract: Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is traditionally conceptualized as a disorder of the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE)-photoreceptor axis; however, this paradigm incompletely explains early disease dynamics and therapeutic failure in geographic atrophy (GA). This review aims to reframe AMD progression through a Müller glial cell-centered framework that integrates cellular homeostasis, structural transitions, and stage-dependent therapeutic implications. Emerging transcriptomic, histologic, and functional evidence demonstrates that Müller glial cells actively participate in AMD pathobiology, including complement regulation, metabolic coupling, redox control, and inflammatory signaling. In early AMD, Müller glial cells exhibit adaptive responses that preserve retinal integrity despite increasing metabolic and extracellular stress. Progressive accumulation of basal laminar deposits and extracellular remodeling may impose diffusion constraints and inflammatory burden, thereby promoting glial reprogramming. A critical transition occurs with descent of the external limiting membrane (ELM), which corresponds to the loss of photoreceptor support, disruption of retinal compartmentalization, and onset of irreversible degeneration. Beyond this threshold, Müller glial cells undergo structural remodeling and contribute to the formation of subretinal glial membranes, reflecting a shift from homeostatic support to containment. This framework proposes a biologically testable staging axis from preserved Müller glial cell function to progressive dysfunction, aligning disease progression with therapeutic windows. Pre-ELM stages are characterized by retained plasticity and suitability for neuroprotective and metabolic interventions, whereas post-ELM stages require strategies focused on stabilization and limiting degeneration. Importantly, most current clinical trials do not explicitly incorporate Müller glial cell state or ELM integrity as stratification variables, potentially contributing to insensitive or diluted outcome assessment. In conclusion, Müller glial cells may function as central integrators of retinal homeostasis and disease progression in AMD. Integrating glial biology with structural biomarkers may enable stage-specific precision therapies and improve clinical trial design.

records.title: Eye-brain axis: Ocular and visual pathophysiology as driver and therapeutic target across the mood disorder trajectory.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Eye-brain axis: Ocular and visual pathophysiology as driver and therapeutic target across the mood disorder trajectory.
content.abstract: In recent years, the promotion of multidisciplinary care and the heightened focus on patients' physical and mental well-being have sparked increased research interest in the mental health burden associated with ophthalmic diseases. In response, we assembled a multidisciplinary team of ophthalmologists, psychiatrists, neurobiologists, and computer scientists to create a systematic and forward-looking overview aimed at guiding future research in both fundamentals of life sciences and brain-computer interface as well as clinical practice. This overview centers on mood disorders, the most prevalent psychiatric conditions among this population. We integrate evidence on the neural, humoral, and inflammatory mechanisms that connect eye disease to mood dysregulation, while also detailing the ocular manifestations typical of mood-disordered patients, including their unique features and underlying mechanisms. Furthermore, we catalog current and emerging ophthalmic and psychiatric diagnostic tools and therapeutic strategies. Finally, we propose a comprehensive multidisciplinary framework for screening, treatment, patient education, and long-term follow-up, providing researchers and clinicians with an evidence-based resource for integrated care.

records.title: Representation of Women Among Individuals With Mild Variants in ABCA4-Associated Retinopathy: A Meta-Analysis.

content.title: Representation of Women Among Individuals With Mild Variants in ABCA4-Associated Retinopathy: A Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Importance

Previous studies indicated that female sex might be a modifier in Stargardt disease, which is an ABCA4-associated retinopathy.

Objective

To investigate whether women are overrepresented among individuals with ABCA4-associated retinopathy who are carrying at least 1 mild allele or carrying nonmild alleles.

Data sources

Literature data, data from 2 European centers, and a new study. Data from a Radboudumc database and from the Rotterdam Eye Hospital were used for exploratory hypothesis testing.

Study selection

Studies investigating the sex ratio in individuals with ABCA4-AR and data from centers that collected ABCA4 variant and sex data. The literature search was performed on February 1, 2023; data from the centers were from before 2023.

Data extraction and synthesis

Random-effects meta-analyses were conducted to test whether the proportions of women among individuals with ABCA4-associated retinopathy with mild and nonmild variants differed from 0.5, including subgroup analyses for mild alleles. Sensitivity analyses were performed excluding data with possibly incomplete variant identification. χ2 Tests were conducted to compare the proportions of women in adult-onset autosomal non-ABCA4-associated retinopathy and adult-onset ABCA4-associated retinopathy and to investigate if women with suspected ABCA4-associated retinopathy are more likely to obtain a genetic diagnosis. Data analyses were performed from March to October 2023.

Main outcomes and measures

Proportion of women per ABCA4-associated retinopathy group. The exploratory testing included sex ratio comparisons for individuals with ABCA4-associated retinopathy vs those with other autosomal retinopathies and for individuals with ABCA4-associated retinopathy who underwent genetic testing vs those who did not.

Results

Women were significantly overrepresented in the mild variant group (proportion, 0.59; 95% CI, 0.56-0.62; P < .001) but not in the nonmild variant group (proportion, 0.50; 95% CI, 0.46-0.54; P = .89). Sensitivity analyses confirmed these results. Subgroup analyses on mild variants showed differences in the proportions of women. Furthermore, in the Radboudumc database, the proportion of adult women among individuals with ABCA4-associated retinopathy (652/1154 = 0.56) was 0.10 (95% CI, 0.05-0.15) higher than among individuals with other retinopathies (280/602 = 0.47).

Conclusions and relevance

This meta-analysis supports the likelihood that sex is a modifier in developing ABCA4-associated retinopathy for individuals with a mild ABCA4 allele. This finding may be relevant for prognosis predictions and recurrence risks for individuals with ABCA4-associated retinopathy. Future studies should further investigate whether the overrepresentation of women is caused by differences in the disease mechanism, by differences in health care-seeking behavior, or by health care discrimination between women and men with ABCA4-AR.

records.title: The role of the choroidal nervous system in central serous chorioretinopathy and associated diseases.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: The role of the choroidal nervous system in central serous chorioretinopathy and associated diseases.
content.abstract: Central serous chorioretinopathy (CSCR) and associated diseases, are linked to abnormal remodeling of the choroidal vasculature, venous congestion and impaired regulation of choroidal blood flow. Although anatomical, genetic and hormonal factors have been identified, a unifying pathophysiological mechanism remains unclear. In this review, we propose that peripheral choroidal nervous system dysfunction may represent a central driver of this choroidal phenotype. First, we provide an updated overview of the organization and functions of the autonomous nervous system, its interaction with the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, as well as the clinical tools used to assess autonomic regulation in humans. We then detail the neurovascular organization of the choroid, highlighting the dense and complex sympathetic, parasympathetic, sensory and intrinsic innervation. Experimental studies demonstrate that not only choroidal blood flow but also immune processes and other aspects of the choroidal environment, are finely regulated by choroidal innervation. Disruption of this neural control induces choroidal vascular enlargement, venous remodeling, inflammation and outer retinal damage, thereby reproducing key features of the choroidal pathology associated with CSCR. Clinical evidence further supports this framework by showing local and systemic autonomic dysregulation in patients with CSCR. This emphasizes the importance of clinical evaluations through pupillometry, heart rate variability, ambulatory blood pressure monitoring, stress biomarkers and dynamic choroidal imaging. Autonomic imbalance also provides a mechanistic link between CSCR and associated risk factors, such as psychological stress, sleep disorders, cardiovascular disease and glucocorticoid exposure.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence in the Multidisciplinary Tumor Board for Prostate Cancer: A Narrative Review.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence in the Multidisciplinary Tumor Board for Prostate Cancer: A Narrative Review.
content.abstract: Multidisciplinary tumor boards (MDTs) guide prostate cancer decisions but are strained by rising case volumes, evolving guidelines, and growing complexity. Artificial intelligence (AI) now enters the MDT at two levels. First, it generates inputs: deep-learning magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) reading matches or exceeds radiologists' performance in the Prostate Imaging-Cancer Artificial Intelligence (PI-CAI) study; Gleason grading reaches expert-level agreement; PSMA PET quantification is automated; and multimodal pathology biomarkers predict ADT benefit. Second, decision-support systems act on MDT output: rule-based tools reproduce standard recommendations in 86-99% of cases, mostly in populations dominated by standard cases, whereas general-purpose large language models (LLMs) agree with real urological boards in 56-93% of cases, depending largely on input quality and case mix, and perform worse in metastatic disease; agreement does not establish clinical benefit. Of 33 appraised decision-support studies, 27 were at high risk of bias, 20 of them solely because the treating board served as an unblinded reference standard; explainability, regulation, and automation bias remain unresolved. We propose that AI currently serves as a supervised pre-reader, guideline checker, and triage tool. Prospective multicenter studies with patient outcomes are needed.

records.title: Assessment of peripapillary choroidal microvascular structure in idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus using a deep learning-based approach.
records.publisher: Graefe's archive for clinical and experimental ophthalmology = Albrecht von Graefes Archiv fur klinische und experimentelle Ophthalmologie

content.title: Assessment of peripapillary choroidal microvascular structure in idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus using a deep learning-based approach.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To investigate peripapillary choroidal microvascular structure in patients with idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus (iNPH) using a novel deep learning-based approach, and to evaluate longitudinal changes following shunt surgery.

Methods

In this prospective study, 22 patients with iNPH and 22 age-matched healthy controls underwent peripapillary optical coherence tomography (OCT). A deep learning-based ResUNet model enabled choroidal segmentation and quantification of total choroidal area (TCA), stromal choroidal area (SCA), luminal choroidal area (LCA), and the choroidal vascularity index (CVI). Measurements were compared between groups and reassessed in iNPH patients after ventriculoperitoneal shunt surgery.

Results

Forty-four eyes of 22 iNPH patients and 44 eyes of 22 controls were analyzed. iNPH eyes exhibited significantly greater mean SCA compared to controls (adjusted p < 0.05). On the other hand, CVI remained comparable between groups. Following a mean follow-up of approximately 12 months after shunt surgery, mean SCA showed significant reduction (adjusted p < 0.05), whereas CVI remained unchanged.

Conclusions

iNPH was associated with peripapillary choroidal changes, predominantly involving the stromal compartment. Deep learning-based OCT analysis may provide a noninvasive approach for quantifying peripapillary choroidal microstructure, although the clinical relevance of these findings remains to be established.

records.title: Early Diagnosis and Prognosis of Corneal and Ocular Surface Pathologies Using Artificial Intelligence: A State-of-the-art Review.

content.title: Early Diagnosis and Prognosis of Corneal and Ocular Surface Pathologies Using Artificial Intelligence: A State-of-the-art Review.
content.abstract:
Purpose

This study aims to elucidate the expanding role of artificial intelligence (AI) in the early diagnosis of corneal and ocular surface diseases. AI has the potential to enhance diagnostic precision, streamline clinical workflows, and facilitate disease detection before clinical manifestations become evident.

Methods

A narrative literature review was conducted to assess the impact of AI and machine learning in corneal disease preclinical diagnosis. A comprehensive search in PubMed was performed using key terms such as "artificial intelligence," "machine learning," "deep learning," "corneal diseases," and "early diagnosis." Eligible studies were those published in English over the last decade that focused on AI-driven diagnostic approaches and prognostic modeling. Case reports, nonoriginal studies, and those with minimal AI integration were excluded. Data extraction emphasized AI methodologies, imaging techniques, diagnostic performance metrics, and clinical relevance.

Results

AI-powered machine learning models analyze vast imaging datasets, detecting subclinical abnormalities imperceptible to conventional diagnostic methods. This capability is particularly significant in early keratoconus detection, dystrophies, infectious keratitis, conjunctival neoplasia, and other corneal pathologies such as dry eye or Steven-Johnson disease, where subtle morphological changes precede clinically apparent disease.

Conclusions

The integration of AI into corneal disease diagnostics and management could mark in the future a transformative shift in Ophthalmology, offering precision, efficiency, and scalability. By facilitating early disease detection and individualized patient assessments, AI minimizes diagnostic inconsistencies and accelerates clinical decision making. Continuous algorithm refinement and real-world validation are crucial to maximizing AI's clinical utility. To fully harness AI's potential, multidisciplinary collaboration among ophthalmologists, data scientists, and regulatory bodies is imperative to address standardization, ethical concerns, and implementation barriers. As AI-driven technologies continue to evolve, they will redefine the standard of care in corneal disease diagnosis, therapeutic precision, and patient outcomes.

records.title: Automating systematic reviews in ophthalmology with the use of large language model deep research tools.

content.title: Automating systematic reviews in ophthalmology with the use of large language model deep research tools.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the performance of large language model (LLM) 'Deep Research' agentic systems for writing systematic reviews (SRs) in ophthalmology.

Methods

Structured prompts were submitted in September 2026 to Deep Research tools powered by GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 to produce SRs on the topics of 50 human-authored SRs published between May and August 2026 in ophthalmology journals (2025 Journal Impact Factor ≥ 3). Main outcomes included literature coverage (recall and precision against the studies included in the human-made SRs on the same topics), data extraction accuracy (discrepant numerical findings against cited sources), percentage of valid references and PRISMA adherence.

Results

One hundred SRs were produced, 50 for each LLM. Both LLMs showed limited overlap with the human-made SRs, with similar recall (38.0% vs. 38.3%; p = 0.859) and higher precision for GPT-6 Astra (53.2% vs. 36.8%; p < 0.001). GPT-6 Astra achieved a lower data reporting error rate (0.2%) compared to Claude Fable 5.1 (0.9%) (p < 0.001). The percentage of valid references was lower for GPT-6 Astra (79.2% vs. 91.4%; p < 0.001). PRISMA adherence was suboptimal for both models (50.2% vs. 55.2% of items fulfilled; p < 0.001).

Conclusion

GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 showed low data reporting error rates in evidence synthesis; however, incomplete literature coverage, bibliography management issues and poor adherence to reporting guidelines mandate human oversight, especially in study selection and quality appraisal.

records.title: Comparative Accuracy of a Commercial Multimodal Large Language Model Versus Clinicians in Dental Age and Sex Estimation from Panoramic Radiographs: A Benchmark Study.

content.title: Comparative Accuracy of a Commercial Multimodal Large Language Model Versus Clinicians in Dental Age and Sex Estimation from Panoramic Radiographs: A Benchmark Study.
content.abstract: Background/Objectives: Routine dental imaging captures cumulative dentoalveolar and periodontal changes, offering a non-invasive window into both chronological aging and physiological senescence. While task-specific deep learning models have been widely explored in dental radiology, the zero-shot diagnostic performance of commercial Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) in adult populations remains underinvestigated. The aim of this study was to benchmark the zero-shot diagnostic accuracy and repeatability of a commercial MLLM against human clinicians of varying experience levels in estimating adult dental age and biological sex from panoramic radiographs (OPGs), using documented chronological age and biological sex as the ground truth. Methods: From 216 initially screened records, this retrospective single-center study included 127 standardized, anonymized OPGs from patients (74 men, 53 women; mean chronological age 55.5 ± 15.8 years, range 18-90 years) treated at the Clinical Department of Cranio-Maxillofacial Surgery, Military Institute of Medicine-National Research Institute in Warsaw. Each radiograph was independently evaluated across three trials by Gemini 3.1 Pro (Google, Mountain View, CA, USA) and once by two clinicians-a maxillofacial specialist (>10 years of experience) and a resident (<3 years of experience)-all blinded to clinical metadata. Results: Gemini 3.1 Pro demonstrated excellent repeatability across the three trials (ICC(A,1) = 0.926, ICC(A,3) = 0.974; p = 0.156) and moderate agreement with chronological age (ICC(A,1) = 0.604), but systematically overestimated age by a mean of 6.23 years. Mean absolute error (MAE) ranged from 12.91 to 13.03 years across the AI trials. The specialist achieved a significantly lower MAE (10.39 years) than all AI assessments (adjusted p ≤ 0.003), whereas the resident (MAE = 11.19 years) did not differ significantly from the AI (adjusted p = 0.282). In biological sex classification the specialist (66.1%) significantly outperformed all three AI trials (41.7-49.6%), while the resident (62.2%) significantly outperformed the first two AI trials (41.7% and 43.3%), but did not differ significantly from the third trial (49.6%). Across all runs, the AI exhibited significant directional asymmetry (p < 0.001), frequently misclassifying male patients as female. Conclusions: While Gemini 3.1 Pro demonstrated high internal repeatability and age-estimation accuracy comparable to a junior resident, its wide limits of agreement, systematic age overestimation, and poor sex-classification accuracy preclude its autonomous use in clinical or forensic workflows. Future studies incorporating healthy control cohorts and validated clinical indices are required to determine whether the observed age overestimation reflects inherent algorithmic miscalibration or sensitivity to cumulative dentoalveolar pathology in hospitalized patients.

records.title: Advances in Multimodal Imaging and Artificial Intelligence for the Diagnosis and Management of Diabetic Retinopathy: From Biomarkers to Personalized Care.

content.title: Advances in Multimodal Imaging and Artificial Intelligence for the Diagnosis and Management of Diabetic Retinopathy: From Biomarkers to Personalized Care.
content.abstract: Background and Objectives: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) remains a leading cause of preventable vision loss. Staging based on colour fundus photography captures only part of a disease that involves the whole neurovascular unit and the retinal periphery. This narrative review summarizes the structural (optical coherence tomography, OCT), vascular (OCT angiography and ultra-widefield imaging) and functional (microperimetry, electrophysiology) biomarkers of DR, grades the evidence supporting each of them, and examines how artificial intelligence (AI) is changing screening, prognostication and treatment selection. Materials and Methods: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus and Web of Science were searched for publications from January 2000 to May 2026, giving priority to randomized trials, prospective multicentre cohorts, systematic reviews and externally validated algorithms. Results: Among imaging biomarkers, disorganization of the retinal inner layers, outer retinal integrity and ultra-widefield angiographic non-perfusion have the most consistent prognostic evidence, whereas OCT angiography metrics remain device-dependent. AI has progressed from research classifiers to autonomous systems with regulatory authorization in the United States and the European Union, to prospectively evaluated deployments in national programmes and low-resource settings, and to time-to-event progression models and foundation models. Image-based prediction improves discrimination over clinical risk factors by modest margins, and biomarker-guided treatment of diabetic macular oedema still rests largely on retrospective series. Cross-device standardization of quantitative metrics, representative datasets, prospective outcome trials and health-economic evidence remain the main gaps. Conclusions: Individualized screening intervals are the application closest to routine practice, whereas phenotype-driven therapy and precision monitoring remain promising but unproven.

records.title: Distinguishing Post-LASIK Ablation Patterns on Corneal Tomography: Comparing Clinician Versus Large Language Model.

content.title: Distinguishing Post-LASIK Ablation Patterns on Corneal Tomography: Comparing Clinician Versus Large Language Model.
content.abstract: Background: The purpose of this study is to assess the ability of generative AI and a refractive surgeon to distinguish post-LASIK Scheimpflug tomography images based on original excimer laser ablation and to recognize untreated corneas. Methods: Corneal tomography Pentacam images from 204 eyes, which included hyperopic ablations, myopic ablations, myopic astigmatic ablations, mixed astigmatic ablations, or untreated eyes, were compiled. These were individually queried in ChatGPT-5.5 using a multiple-choice prompt to obtain a response. A refractive surgeon was also tested on the same 204 corneas. Results: The clinician obtained higher overall accuracy (85.8% [95% CI 80.2-90.3]) compared to ChatGPT, (60.3% [95% CI 53.2-67.1], p < 0.001) and was significantly more likely to answer correctly overall based on McNemar's test. Additionally, ChatGPT underperformed in the myopia with astigmatism, mixed astigmatism, and untreated categories, with sensitivities of 38%, 6.3%, and 76%, respectively. Conclusions: The overall accuracy of ChatGPT-5.5 did not meet that of the clinician while ability to identify myopic and hyperopic ablation patterns was comparable. Both the AI model and the clinician had decreased accuracy in myopic astigmatism and mixed astigmatism ablation patterns, though the clinician still performed significantly better. Further studies involving alternative AI models, multicenter data, and standardized evaluation protocols are warranted to establish the clinical applicability of these findings.

records.title: An intelligent systems framework for closed-loop chronic glaucoma management.
records.publisher: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology

content.title: An intelligent systems framework for closed-loop chronic glaucoma management.
content.abstract:
Background

Glaucoma, the world's leading cause of irreversible blindness, highlights chronic disease management challenges: fragmented health records, poor adherence, and limited privacy safeguards. While artificial intelligence (AI) shows promise, its clinical application remains confined to isolated algorithmic tasks.

Methods

To bridge the gap, GlauHelper, an internet-based platform integrating multiple AI modules, is developed. The dual-end (physician/patient) platform integrates a comprehensive clinical workflow: (1) Secure Data Acquisition, featuring age-friendly interfaces, home-based tonometer, and an image privacy system; (2) Automated Processing Pipeline, which cleans and structures real-world uploads through quality scoring, cascaded classification, and data extraction, with human verification; and (3) Clinical Application, utilizing structured data to drive personalized follow-up, medication tracking, and a domain-specific Large Language Model (LLM) Q&A assistant ("Xiaoqing") optimized for glaucoma education.

Results

Real-world deployment across 30 hospitals and over 10,000 users in China demonstrated high adoption. Experimental validation confirmed the system's ability to extract structured clinical data, safeguard patient privacy, assess and classify medical images, and deliver educational content.

Conclusion

GlauHelper demonstrates the technical feasibility of integrating secure data acquisition, automated information processing, and patient-clinician interaction within a unified glaucoma management workflow. These findings support its preliminary usability and real-world deployability, while its effects on treatment adherence, disease progression, and long-term clinical outcomes require further prospective evaluation.

records.title: Explainable CNN Ensemble with AI-Generated Reporting for Fungal Infection Diagnosis.

content.title: Explainable CNN Ensemble with AI-Generated Reporting for Fungal Infection Diagnosis.
content.abstract: The need for precise classification of fungi from microscopic images plays a critical role in diagnosing and treating patients since it requires timeliness and effectiveness. Nevertheless, manual examination is time-consuming and difficult due to the similar visual features of numerous fungi. Therefore, this work proposes a new approach to explainable deep learning for fungal image classification and report generation. The developed framework consists of four pre-trained convolutional neural network models-DenseNet121, ResNet18, VGG16, and InceptionV3-which are used to classify fungal microscopic images into five classes. To make the process more transparent, methods such as Grad-CAM, SHAP, LIME, and Canny edge detection are used to identify the areas of images that contribute to the prediction. At the same time, the developed approach uses the large language model LLaMA3-70B through LangChain and provides automatic generation of the structured diagnostic report, including fungal identification, confidence scores, and clinical observations. The whole pipeline is implemented using the Streamlit interface to predict and generate a PDF report of the classification. The experiments have been performed using publicly available data containing 5000 images of fungi with expert annotations. Among the models analyzed, DenseNet121 shows the highest result, reaching an accuracy of 99.75% and having the values of precision, recall, and F1-score close to 0.998.

records.title: MCG-Net: Multiscale Residual Context Learning for Retinal OCT Classification with External Model Comparison.

content.title: MCG-Net: Multiscale Residual Context Learning for Retinal OCT Classification with External Model Comparison.
content.abstract: Background and Objectives: Retinal optical coherence tomography (OCT) classification requires recognition of subtle lesions within their anatomical surroundings, yet expanding contextual coverage can obscure local structural information. MCG-Net integrates local morphology and multiscale context within a gated convolutional hierarchy. Methods: A retained depthwise local pathway is augmented by two compressed separable context branches with bounded channel-wise residual scales. This study distinguishes choroidal neovascularization, diabetic macular edema, drusen, and normal retina. OCT-C8 provides development images; independent CAVRI-H5 and OCTDL datasets provide 384 external observations. Both external datasets remain excluded from parameter fitting, development validation, and checkpoint selection, but their ablation results inform selection of the Full 11/23 architecture. Paired comparisons, source-specific assessment, and visual error analysis characterize this external model comparison. Results: MCG-Net achieved 92.01±0.60% accuracy, 91.99±0.61% macro-F1, and 89.47±0.80% Matthews correlation coefficient. Combined context improved macro-F1 over the local baseline by 2.18 percentage points, with a paired 98% interval of 0.50-4.04 and adjusted p=0.019. Exploratory comparisons identified differences against six alternatives, while advantages over the strongest comparators remained uncertain. Source-specific accuracy was 90.86% on CAVRI-H5 and 95.49% on OCTDL; drusen remained the most difficult category. The model contains 26.82 million parameters and has 4.28 ms median inference latency on an RTX 5090. Conclusions: Compressed residual context strengthens gated convolutional OCT classification without replacing local processing. Reuse of the external cohort for architecture selection limits confirmatory interpretation. Untouched external validation, complete-development patient metadata, and representative clinical sampling are needed before clinical use.

records.title: Association between deep-learning-derived retinal aging speed and rapid decline of renal function in the Japanese general population.

content.title: Association between deep-learning-derived retinal aging speed and rapid decline of renal function in the Japanese general population.
content.abstract:
Background

The eye and the kidney share microvascular features, and retinal changes have been postulated to reflect systemic cardiometabolic dysfunction. Recently, retinal age, estimated by deep learning (DL) from a single fundus photograph, has been shown to predict cardiovascular events. The present study aimed to determine whether retinal aging speed, defined as the individual-specific annual rate of change in DL-estimated retinal age, is associated with rapid estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) decline.

Methods

We retrospectively analyzed the longitudinal data obtained from 7807 Japanese individuals who underwent repeated health check-ups with serial measurements of eGFR and fundus photographs (median 9.0 visits over median 8.0 years). We evaluated the relationship between retinal aging speed during the baseline period (from baseline to year 4) and rapid eGFR decline (≤ -3 ml/min/1.73 m²/year) during the follow-up period (after year 4).

Results

The incidence of rapid eGFR decline was significantly higher in the highest quartile of retinal aging speed than in the lowest quartile as the reference group in the fully adjusted model adjusting age, sex, body mass index, blood pressure, diabetes, smoking, eGFR, and proteinuria [odds ratio (OR) 1.34; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.06-1.68; P = .015]. In the multivariable logistic regression models, retinal aging speed was associated with rapid eGFR decline after adjusting multiple key confounders (OR 1.14; 95% CI 1.02-1.29; P = .027).

Conclusions

Taken together, DL-derived retinal aging speed is independently associated with rapid eGFR decline in the Japanese general population.

records.title: Mapping Research on AI-Based Computer-Aided Diagnosis and Clinical Decision Support Systems: a Bibliometric Study Integrating Google Trends and Content Analysis.

content.title: Mapping Research on AI-Based Computer-Aided Diagnosis and Clinical Decision Support Systems: a Bibliometric Study Integrating Google Trends and Content Analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Research on artificial intelligence-based computer-aided diagnosis and clinical decision support systems (AI-CDSS) is expanding, but integrated evidence on publication patterns, keyword trajectories, online search activity, and methodological characteristics remains limited.

Objective

To characterize AI-CDSS research by integrating bibliometric analysis, Google Trends comparison, and structured content analysis of citation-ranked publications.

Methods

Scholarly interest was assessed using bibliometric analysis of Web of Science records from 2016 through August 2026, including author-keyword co-occurrence, bibliographic coupling, and reference co-citation, whereas Google Trends was used to characterize online search activity. A structured content analysis of citation-ranked publications was conducted to examine applications, methodological characteristics, and reported limitations.

Results

We analyzed 19,809 included publications from 2016 through August 2026. Output rose approximately 21-fold, from 193 records in 2016 to 4,082 in 2025. Output was geographically concentrated within the included corpus, with a Gini coefficient of 0.869. Among records with identifiable corresponding-author country or territory, China, the United States, and India accounted for 61.33%. Scientific Reports was the most frequent source (n = 916). Frequent artificial intelligence- and diagnosis-related keywords included machine learning (n = 5,666), deep learning (n = 4,022), and computer-aided diagnosis (n = 1,512). Bibliographic coupling identified 15 publication communities, and reference co-citation identified seven reference communities. In the monthly level-series comparison, 9 of 10 keyword concepts exhibited significant associations with Google Trends relative search interest, but none of the 10 first-difference associations remained significant after Bonferroni adjustment. Content analysis of 215 citation-ranked publications, including 191 empirical publications, showed frequent use of convolutional neural networks in diagnostic and radiology applications. Common limitations included limited external validation, infrequent calibration reporting, and sparse workflow-level or impact evaluation.

Conclusion

AI-CDSS research has rapidly expanded around machine learning, deep learning, and diagnostic applications, but the analyzed citation-ranked publications provide more evidence of methodological development than of clinical deployment. Integrating bibliometric, search-activity, and content-based perspectives shows limited short-term correspondence between online search activity and scholarly keyword use and highlights the need to move beyond model development toward independent external validation, prospective workflow and patient-outcome evaluation, calibration, fairness, and postdeployment monitoring.

records.title: DeepSkin: A Segmentation-Guided Deep Learning Framework with Generative Augmentation for Dermoscopic Skin Cancer Classification.

content.title: DeepSkin: A Segmentation-Guided Deep Learning Framework with Generative Augmentation for Dermoscopic Skin Cancer Classification.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence has considerable potential to support dermoscopic skin cancer assessment; however, class imbalance, heterogeneous lesion morphology, indistinct lesion boundaries, and imaging variability can limit model generalizability. This study presents DeepSkin, a segmentation-guided deep learning framework integrating lesion segmentation, generative augmentation, and lesion-focused classification. Dermoscopic images were first segmented using a bidirectional ConvLSTM-based U-Net (BCDU-Net), and the resulting lesion regions were used for region-of-interest (ROI) extraction. During classifier development, a conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN) generated class-conditioned synthetic lesion ROIs to increase training-data diversity and mitigate class imbalance. Real and synthetic training ROIs were subsequently used to train a fine-tuned VGG16 network for binary benign-malignant classification. The framework was developed using the ISIC 2016 dataset, comprising 900 training and 379 test images, and independently evaluated on the PH2 dataset. On ISIC 2016, DeepSkin achieved a Dice coefficient of 0.937 and an intersection over union (IoU) of 0.882 for lesion segmentation, together with a classification accuracy of 96.6% and a receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC-AUC) of 0.981. Cross-dataset external evaluation on the independent PH2 dataset, conducted without retraining or fine-tuning, yielded a classification accuracy of 95%. Ablation analysis further demonstrated incremental performance improvements associated with preprocessing, segmentation-guided ROI extraction, and generative augmentation. Grad-CAM visualizations provided qualitative insight into image regions contributing to classification decisions. These findings suggest that integrating generative augmentation with segmentation-guided lesion classification can support accurate dermoscopic image analysis across independent datasets. Further evaluation using larger, diverse, multi-center and prospective clinical datasets is required to establish broader generalizability and clinical applicability.

records.title: Comparison of Retinopathy Screening Performed Using Conventional Methods and an Artificial Intelligence-Assisted System in Prediabetic and Diabetic Patients: A Single-Center Prospective Analysis.

content.title: Comparison of Retinopathy Screening Performed Using Conventional Methods and an Artificial Intelligence-Assisted System in Prediabetic and Diabetic Patients: A Single-Center Prospective Analysis.
content.abstract: Background and Objectives: AI-assisted retinal imaging is increasingly proposed to expand diabetic retinopathy (DR) screening capacity, but most validation studies use reading-center standards, exclude prediabetes, and assess macular edema against photographic surrogates rather than optical coherence tomography (OCT). We compared an AI-assisted retinal screening system with routine ophthalmological examination in an unselected internal medicine screening population. Materials and Methods: In this prospective, cross-sectional diagnostic accuracy study, consecutive adults with prediabetes or diabetes underwent AI-assisted retinal imaging (index test) followed by masked ophthalmological examination (reference standard), with OCT as the reference for macular edema. Analyses were performed at the eye level (n = 714) and patient level (n = 357) using Wilson score 95% confidence intervals and Cohen kappa (κ) for agreement. Results: Among 357 patients (714 eyes; 83.8% diabetes, 16.2% prediabetes), DR prevalence by ophthalmological examination was 15.0% (eyes) and 17.9% (patients), versus 24.4% and 33.1% by AI (McNemar p < 0.001). Eye-level and patient-level sensitivity and specificity were 70.1% and 83.7% and 75.0% and 76.1%, respectively. Negative predictive value was high (93-94%) but positive predictive value was low (41-43%); agreement was moderate at the eye level and fair at the patient level (κ = 0.428 and 0.384, respectively). False-positive AI calls were associated with higher HbA1c and albuminuria (adjusted odds ratio for log-transformed ACR 1.23, p = 0.040); false negatives had milder disease. In prediabetes, DR prevalence was 1.7% and agreement was absent (κ = -0.03). AI sensitivity for OCT-defined macular edema was 45.5% (κ = 0.197), with no significant central macular thickness difference by AI status. Conclusions: The AI system showed high negative predictive value but systematically over-called DR, with only fair-to-moderate agreement and performance below accepted screening benchmarks, particularly in prediabetes and for macular edema. These findings support its use as a rule-out triage adjunct with ophthalmological confirmation of positive results, rather than an autonomous substitute, and argue for local recalibration before deployment.

records.title: Automated assessment of healthcare de-escalation communication skills in a conversational AI virtual reality simulation.

content.title: Automated assessment of healthcare de-escalation communication skills in a conversational AI virtual reality simulation.
content.abstract:
Introduction

Digital health training environments increasingly require scalable methods for assessing communication skills in realistic, interactive scenarios. This paper presents a comparative study of automated assessment approaches within a conversational AI virtual reality simulation designed for verbal de-escalation training.

Methods

A total of 20 nursing students completed the simulation, where their spoken responses were captured and converted to text through a speech-to-text system, and were evaluated across 11 de-escalation competencies. The evaluation compared three fine-tuned deep learning models (BERT, RoBERTa, and XLNet) with a modified RATAS, a rubric-driven framework that leverages large language models. Two experiments were conducted: one using controlled 100-item validation datasets for each section, and another using the real-world responses collected during the user study.

Results

On the validation datasets, the deep learning models achieved the highest performance, with RoBERTa obtaining an average accuracy of 0.9927, followed by BERT at 0.9900 and XLNet at 0.9790, while RATAS achieved 0.8554. On the student-response dataset, performance decreased for all approaches, with RoBERTa obtaining 0.8590 accuracy, RATAS 0.8181, BERT 0.8000, and XLNet 0.7681.

Discussion

These results suggest that transformer-based models perform best under controlled conditions, whereas RATAS demonstrated stability in grading across different dataset types. These preliminary findings support the feasibility of integrating deep learning and rubric-driven LLM-based automated assessment approaches for communication and de-escalation training in nursing education.

records.title: Global research trends of artificial intelligence in echocardiography (1984-2025): a bibliometric analysis.

content.title: Global research trends of artificial intelligence in echocardiography (1984-2025): a bibliometric analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Echocardiography has evolved substantially since its introduction in 1954. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers transformative potential for image acquisition, quantification, interpretation, and reporting. Despite growing research interest, a comprehensive evaluation of the historical trends and evolution of AI in echocardiography is lacking. The study aimed to conduct a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of the global research landscape in this field.

Methods

A systematic literature search was conducted using the Scopus and Web of Science Core Collection databases for publications on AI in echocardiography from inception through November 10, 2025; no language filter was applied. Data analysis was performed using Microsoft Excel, Microsoft Access, and IBM SPSS Statistics. In addition, bibliometric mapping and data visualization were conducted.

Results

Overall, 2682 publications received 35,083 citations (mean, 13.08 citations per publication), spanning 1984-2025. Original articles, conference papers, and review articles accounted for 87.4% and 98.5% of total publications and citations, respectively. Publication output remained limited until approximately 2015, rose gradually thereafter, and accelerated markedly after 2018, with similar output in 2024 and 2025. The United States led in both publication volume and total citations, followed by China and the United Kingdom. The United States also had the highest collaboration link strength, and seven of the top 10 institutions were in North America (six in the United States and one in Canada). Mayo Clinic ranked first, with 142 publications and 3604 citations, and had the earliest first indexed publication among the top institutions (1992). The journal JACC: Cardiovascular Imaging ranked first in both total citations (1,911) and citations per publication (36.75). "Echocardiography," "deep learning," "artificial intelligence," and "machine learning" were the most frequently used terms. The thematic evolution showed continuity of algorithmic-centric themes (1984-2019) with emerging clinically oriented themes (2020-2025).

Conclusions

This comprehensive bibliometric analysis highlights the rapid expansion of AI research in echocardiography, characterized by an accelerating publication output and emerging clinically oriented research topics. These findings reflect growing research interest in integrating AI into echocardiographic practice and highlight the need for future research prioritizing multicenter validation, clinical translation, and equitable real-world implementation.

records.title: Beyond scales: Artificial intelligence, language, and behavior in suicide risk modeling-a narrative review.
records.publisher: European neuropsychopharmacology : the journal of the European College of Neuropsychopharmacology

content.title: Beyond scales: Artificial intelligence, language, and behavior in suicide risk modeling-a narrative review.
content.abstract: Suicide is a leading, preventable cause of premature mortality, yet identifying individuals at imminent risk remains difficult. There are no validated biomarkers for routine stratification, and common approaches (clinical interviews, rating scales, self-report) are limited by subjectivity, reporting bias, and weak positive predictive value for rare outcomes. Rapid advances in artificial intelligence (AI)-including machine learning, deep learning, and large language models-offer opportunities to integrate heterogeneous signals relevant to risk and treatment response. This narrative review summarizes recent AI-enabled prediction and characterization of suicidal thoughts and behaviors across major data modalities: structured electronic health records and claims; natural language processing of clinical notes and digital text; speech and facial/behavioral signals; neuroimaging and other neurobiological measures; and passive sensing from smartphones and wearables. We review common modeling and evaluation practices, emphasizing clinically relevant performance assessment (discrimination and calibration) and the importance of temporal and external validation. We also highlight barriers to translation, including class imbalance and label noise, dataset shift across sites and time, limited prospective evaluation, and the need for interpretable outputs that can support medication decisions and care pathways (e.g., triage, monitoring, and stepped interventions). Ethical and implementation challenges-privacy and consent, algorithmic bias and equity, governance, and the clinical consequences of false-positive and false-negative predictions-are discussed with an emphasis on safe deployment. We conclude with priorities for the field, including multimodal longitudinal cohorts, harmonized reporting standards, and pragmatic trials to determine whether AI decision support measurably improves suicide-prevention outcomes.

records.title: Application of an Artificial Intelligence Simulated Patient Model in Teaching Neurosurgical Decision-Making.

content.title: Application of an Artificial Intelligence Simulated Patient Model in Teaching Neurosurgical Decision-Making.
content.abstract:
Aim

Training in neurosurgical decision-making remains a challenging component of standardized residency training. Traditional teaching models are limited in their ability to simulate the uncertainty and complexity encountered in real-world clinical scenarios. As a novel educational tool, the potential value of artificial intelligence (AI)-simulated patient models in surgical decision-making training requires further evaluation. This study aimed to explore the application of an AI-simulated patient model in neurosurgical decision-making education and to assess its effectiveness in improving residents' clinical decision-making abilities.

Methods

A retrospective study was conducted involving 157 residents who underwent standardized residency training in the Department of Neurosurgery from January 2023 to April 2026. Based on the implementation of the AI-simulated teaching model beginning in January 2025, participants were divided into two groups according to the teaching model used: an experimental group (n = 72, receiving AI-simulated patient teaching from January 2025 to April 2026) and a control group (n = 85, receiving traditional case discussion teaching from January 2023 to December 2024). The experimental group used a large language model-based virtual patient system powered by DeepSeek to perform dialogue-driven history taking, image interpretation, surgical planning, and risk prediction with real-time feedback, while the control group received conventional methods. After teaching, an objective structured clinical examination (OSCE) was used to assess surgical decision-making across five dimensions, including localization diagnosis, surgical approach, risk identification, emergency management, and surgical timing, and a questionnaire was used to measure teaching satisfaction.

Results

The total score for surgical decision-making ability was significantly higher in the experimental group than in the control group (p < 0.001). Dimensional analysis showed that localization diagnosis, surgical method selection, risk identification, emergency response, and surgical timing judgment were higher in the experimental group than in the control group (all p < 0.05). The excellent rate for each assessment dimension (>85 points) was significantly higher in the experimental group than in the control group (p < 0.05). The satisfaction score was also higher in the experimental group than in the control group (p < 0.001).

Conclusions

The AI-simulated patient model based on a general-purpose large language model was associated with better surgical decision-making performance among neurosurgery residents. It has significant advantages in localization diagnosis, surgical approach selection, risk identification, emergency response, and judgment of surgical timing, and is well accepted by residents.

records.title: Beyond the Chatbot: Agentic Artificial Intelligence and the Future of Infectious Disease Practice.
records.publisher: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America

content.title: Beyond the Chatbot: Agentic Artificial Intelligence and the Future of Infectious Disease Practice.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) discourse in infectious disease (ID) has focused on benchmarking large language model chatbots against clinicians, a useful but narrowing inquiry. Agentic AI is a different paradigm: goal-directed systems that pursue clinical objectives over time, integrating data, invoking tools, monitoring results, and adapting without repeated prompting. This Viewpoint defines the anatomy of an agent, situates it within a 3-level framework (predictive, conversational, agentic), and examines how agents could transform 6 domains of ID practice: clinical care, antimicrobial stewardship, clinical microbiology, infection prevention and control, research, and epidemiology and pandemic preparedness. Individual components have proven value; integrated systems remain untested. No validated agentic system has been deployed in clinical ID; error propagation, algorithmic bias, cost, absent validation frameworks, undefined liability, and consequences for the workforce and its training must be addressed first. The ID community has a narrow window to shape these systems before decisions are made without it.

records.title: Impact of Image Bit Depth Reduction on Deep Learning Performance in Chest Radiograph Analysis: A Multi-institutional Study.

content.title: Impact of Image Bit Depth Reduction on Deep Learning Performance in Chest Radiograph Analysis: A Multi-institutional Study.
content.abstract:
Rationale and objectives

Medical imaging typically generates 12-bit to 16-bit formats, yet conversion to 8-bit is often required. While deep learning has been widely explored in medical imaging, the influence of image bit depth on model performance is not fully understood. This study evaluates the impact of conversion from 16-bit to 8-bit for sex, age, and obesity classification using deep learning.

Materials and methods

In this retrospective, multi-institutional study, we analyzed 100,002 chest radiographs from 48,047 participants across three institutions. Images were uniformly quantized from the fixed 0-65535 range to 256 levels (0-255) with no additional processing. Three convolutional neural network architectures (ResNet52, EfficientNetB2, and ConvNeXtSmall) were trained on both 16-bit and 8-bit versions of the images. Model performance was evaluated using internal test datasets, randomly split multiple times, and an external test dataset. Statistical analysis included paired comparisons of area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) values, with Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons.

Results

Across all architectures and classification tasks, differences between 16-bit and 8-bit model performance were minimal (mean differences ranging from -0.218%-0.184%). Statistical analyses revealed no significant differences in AUC-ROC values between bit depths for any model-task combination (all p values > 0.05 after Bonferroni correction). Effect sizes were small to moderate (Cohen's d ranging from -0.415-0.391).

Conclusion

No statistically significant differences were detected between models trained on 16-bit and 8-bit images in the three evaluated tasks. These findings suggest that conversion to 8-bit images may reduce data storage requirements and improve data processing efficiency. Further research is needed to assess their usefulness in clinical tasks.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence in Breast Cancer Diagnosis, Treatment, and Perioperative Management: A Systematic Review of Current Applications and Future Perspectives.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence in Breast Cancer Diagnosis, Treatment, and Perioperative Management: A Systematic Review of Current Applications and Future Perspectives.
content.abstract:
Background

Breast cancer is the most frequently diagnosed malignancy in women globally, accounting for approximately 2.30 million new cases and 666,103 deaths in 2022. Artificial intelligence technologies including machine learning, deep learning, radiomics, and natural language processing have been widely applied across the breast cancer care continuum. However, no systematic review restricted to primary studies with patient-level or image-level data has synthesized evidence spanning all clinical domains simultaneously.

Objectives

To evaluate the performance, methodological quality, and clinical relevance of artificial intelligence primary studies across screening and diagnostic imaging, digital pathology, radiomics, perioperative management, prognostic prediction, and natural language processing in breast cancer.

Methods

PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from January 2015 to May 2026. Eligibility was restricted to original primary research reporting patient-level or image-level data; secondary syntheses were explicitly excluded. Risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-2 and PROBAST. Reporting followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines.

Results

Of 5,275 identified records, 17 primary studies met eligibility criteria. In screening mammography (seven studies; n = 7,540 to 144,231 examinations), deep learning achieved area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values of 0.876 to 0.939; a randomised trial in 80,033 women demonstrated non-inferiority to double reading with a 44.3% reduction in radiologist workload. In digital pathology (five studies; 270 to 44,732 whole-slide images), deep learning achieved AUC 0.985 to 0.994, exceeding unassisted pathologist performance in lymph node metastasis detection. Magnetic resonance imaging radiomics predicted pathological complete response in HER2-positive breast cancer with AUC 0.80. No breast cancer-specific perioperative primary study met the eligibility criteria. Deep survival networks achieved concordance index 0.626 versus 0.612 for Cox regression in breast cancer cohorts. Natural language processing identified metastatic recurrence in breast cancer clinical records with sensitivity 83% and specificity 73%. Risk of bias was low to moderate for imaging and pathology studies and high for small sample radiomics studies. Density-stratified performance was reported by only two imaging studies, and receptor status prediction from haematoxylin and eosin staining had not been validated as a safe alternative to immunohistochemistry.

Conclusions

Artificial intelligence demonstrated clinically meaningful performance across the five domains with eligible primary studies. Breast cancer-specific perioperative and intensive care primary studies were absent, representing the largest evidence gap. External validation, demographic diversity, and prospective clinical integration evidence remained the most consistently identified limitations. Prediction of molecular receptor status without immunohistochemistry requires rigorous prospective safety validation before it can complement standard testing.

records.title: From inherited susceptibility to tumor state: toward a stage-aware architecture for genomic risk stratification in prostate cancer.

content.title: From inherited susceptibility to tumor state: toward a stage-aware architecture for genomic risk stratification in prostate cancer.
content.abstract: Prostate cancer risk is currently represented by two largely separate genomic layers. Germline polygenic scores estimate inherited susceptibility before diagnosis, whereas tumor genomic and transcriptomic classifiers estimate biological aggressiveness and treatment response after tissue acquisition. Artificial intelligence can connect these layers, but simply concatenating high-dimensional features is unlikely to produce transportable clinical tools. This Mini Review examines how biologically informed machine learning, single-cell and spatial atlases, whole-omics response models, and validated tissue classifiers are reshaping prostate cancer risk stratification. We argue that the most useful architecture is a stage-aware system: ancestry-calibrated germline risk first modifies screening intensity; tissue or liquid-biopsy models then resolve tumor state; and longitudinal molecular measurements update risk under treatment. Evidence is strongest for polygenic enrichment of screening populations and for locked transcriptomic classifiers tested in randomized-trial cohorts. By contrast, many multi-omics models remain retrospective, dataset-dependent, and weakly calibrated across ancestry, disease stage, and specimen type. Progress requires explicit clinical decision points, external and prospective validation, uncertainty reporting, ancestry-aware calibration, and comparisons against simpler clinicopathological models. A unified framework should therefore treat artificial intelligence not as a single prognostic score, but as an auditable sequence of genomic updates that links inherited susceptibility to evolving tumor biology.

records.title: Radiomics for differentiating radiation-induced brain injury from recurrence in gliomas: systematic review, meta-analysis, and methodological quality evaluation using METRICS and RQS.

content.title: Radiomics for differentiating radiation-induced brain injury from recurrence in gliomas: systematic review, meta-analysis, and methodological quality evaluation using METRICS and RQS.
content.abstract:
Objective

To systematically evaluate glioma radiomics literature on differentiating between radiation-induced brain injury and tumor recurrence.

Methods

Literature was searched on PubMed and Web of Science (end date: May 7, 2024). Quality of eligible papers was assessed using METhodological RadiomICs Score (METRICS) and Radiomics Quality Score (RQS). Reliability of quality scoring tools were analyzed. Meta-analysis, meta-regression, and subgroup analysis were performed.

Results

Twenty-seven papers were included in the qualitative assessment. Mean average METRICS score and RQS percentage score across three readers was 57% (SD, 14%) and 16% (SD, 12%), respectively. Score-wise inter-rater agreement for METRICS ranged from poor to excellent, while RQS demonstrated moderate to excellent agreement. Item-wise agreement was moderate for both tools. Meta-analysis of 11 eligible studies yielded an estimated area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.832 (95% CI, 0.757-0.908), with significant heterogeneity (I2 = 91%) and no statistical publication bias (p = 0.051). Meta-regression did not identify potential sources of heterogeneity. Subgroup analysis revealed high heterogeneity across all subgroups, with the lowest I2 at 68% in studies with proper validation and higher quality scores. Statistical publication bias was generally not significant, except in the subgroup with the lowest heterogeneity (p = 0.044). However, most studies in both qualitative analysis (26/27; 96%) and primary meta-analysis (10/11; 91%) reported positive effects of radiomics, indicating high non-statistical publication bias.

Conclusion

While a good performance was noted for radiomics, results should be interpreted cautiously due to heterogeneity, publication bias, and quality issues thoroughly examined in this study.

Key points

Question Radiomic literature on distinguishing radiation-induced brain injury from glioma recurrence lacks systematic reviews and meta-analyses that assess methodological quality using radiomics-specific tools. Findings While the results are encouraging, there was substantial heterogeneity, publication bias toward positive findings, and notable concerns regarding methodological quality. Clinical relevance Meta-analysis results need cautious interpretation due to significant problems detected during the analysis (e.g., suboptimal quality, heterogeneity, bias), which may help explain why radiomics has not yet been translated into clinical practice.

records.title: Integrative Multi-Omics in Glaucoma: Defining Mechanistic Axes and Enabling Precision Management.

content.title: Integrative Multi-Omics in Glaucoma: Defining Mechanistic Axes and Enabling Precision Management.
content.abstract: Glaucoma is increasingly recognized not as a uniform pressure-defined optic neuropathy, but rather as a heterogeneous neurodegenerative disorder driven by interacting genetic, metabolic, mechanical, vascular, inflammatory, and environmental factors. Although genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics have each yielded important insights, no single omics layer can fully capture the multilevel architecture underlying differences in disease susceptibility, progression, and treatment response. Multi-omics therefore offers a more integrated framework for linking inherited risk, gene regulation, cellular states, protein activity, metabolic vulnerability, and imaging phenotypes to clinically relevant outcomes. This review summarizes recent advances in multi-omics research in glaucoma, spanning genomics, epigenomics and transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics and lipidomics, microbiome studies, and emerging approaches such as spatial omics, single-cell multi-omics, radiomics, and exposomics. We further discuss how cross-layer integration, network analysis, Mendelian randomization, imaging genomics, and multimodal artificial intelligence are helping to define convergent pathogenic pathways and clinically relevant molecular subtypes. Particular attention is given to four major pathological axes: extracellular matrix-mechanical stress, mitochondrial-metabolic dysfunction, immune-microbiome dysregulation, and exposure-vascular burden. Despite ongoing challenges in standardization, cohort size, validation, and interpretability, multi-omics is shifting glaucoma research toward mechanism-based stratification and deployable precision care.

records.title: Deep learning classification models demonstrate high accuracy and clinical potential in radiograph interpretation in the arthroplasty clinical pathway: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

content.title: Deep learning classification models demonstrate high accuracy and clinical potential in radiograph interpretation in the arthroplasty clinical pathway: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

Imaging is a cornerstone of the osteoarthritis (OA)-arthroplasty clinical pathway: the continuum of care that patients with OA undergo, from initial diagnosis through to arthroplasty and postoperative follow-up. With growing interest from the orthopaedic community, this meta-analysis broadly evaluates the performance of deep learning algorithms in interpreting radiographs and cross-sectional imaging in this pathway. The authors hypothesise that deep learning algorithms will have comparable performance to clinicians when interpreting radiographs, but not cross-sectional imaging, with negligible difference in diagnostic and prognostic tasks.

Methods

Ovid Medline, Ovid Embase, Scopus and Web of Science were searched for studies published between January 1, 2012, and April 1, 2024, evaluating deep learning algorithms for diagnostic and prognostic tasks along the pathway. Eligible studies included those that used established diagnostic or surgical candidacy assessments as ground truth. Study quality was assessed using the Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies 2 tool, and pooled sensitivity and specificity were determined. Hierarchical summary receiver operating characteristic curves assessed diagnostic performance.

Results

The meta-analysis of artificial intelligence (AI) interpretation included 66 studies, with a pooled sensitivity of 0.88 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.81-0.92) and a pooled specificity of 0.91 (95% CI: 0.87-0.94). Sensitivity and specificity values were higher for AI interpretation of radiographs (55 studies) compared to cross-sectional imaging, with no significant difference in performance between diagnostic and prognostic tasks.
