Exercise reduced alanine aminotransferase (ALT; MD -7.33 U/L, 95% CI -10.71 to -3.95), aspartate aminotransferase (AST; MD -5.52 U/L, 95% CI -10.24 to -0.79), and BMI (random-effects MD -1.54 kg/m², 95% CI -2.28 to -0.80), and improved VO2peak/VO2max (MD 4.08 mL/kg/min, 95% CI 1.00 to 7.16). Pooled effects for liver fat/steatosis, HOMA-IR, and HbA1c were not statistically significant. Egger testing showed no significant asymmetry for ALT or AST, whereas BMI showed funnel-plot asymmetry consistent with possible small-study effects.

Conclusion

Exercise training improves hepatic enzymes, BMI, and cardiorespiratory fitness in adults with MASLD/NAFLD, whereas evidence for liver fat and glycemic outcomes remains less certain. PROSPERO: CRD420261416397.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420261416397.

records.title: Whole-mount histopathology as spatial ground truth for artificial intelligence in prostate cancer: a structured narrative review of techniques, models, and translational gaps.
records.publisher: American journal of clinical and experimental urology

content.title: Whole-mount histopathology as spatial ground truth for artificial intelligence in prostate cancer: a structured narrative review of techniques, models, and translational gaps.
content.abstract:
Background

Prostate cancer is spatially heterogeneous, multifocal, and architecturally varied. Conventional biopsy and step-sectioned histopathology fragment the gland. This limits accurate assessment of dominant-lesion identity, tumor volume, multifocality, extraprostatic extension, seminal vesicle invasion, and surgical margin status. Whole-mount histopathology (WMH) preserves the prostate as a continuous cross-sectional unit and is increasingly used as the reference standard for radiology-pathology correlation and for validating artificial-intelligence (AI) models.

Objective

This structured narrative review synthesizes evidence on the joint use of WMH and AI in prostate cancer pathology. For each clinical question, we examine what spatial information WMH preserves, what AI methods extract from that information, where the joint approach has been validated, and where validation gaps remain. The questions are index-lesion identification, tumor-volume estimation, multifocality, extraprostatic extension, seminal vesicle invasion, surgical margin assessment, Gleason grading, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-pathology registration, and surgical quality assurance.

Findings

WMH improves index-lesion identification, volumetric reproducibility, and margin clarity, and provides a high-fidelity reference standard for training prostate-AI models. Registered to the patient's presurgical MRI, these whole-mount labels have also been used to train preoperative tools and have been studied in research cohorts for focal-therapy margin definition and extraprostatic-extension prediction, extending the value of WMH beyond retrospective staging. AI systems built on WMH show improved performance for tumor detection and Gleason classification. Most reported results, however, lack external validation, reporting against established medical-AI standards, and demonstrated robustness across scanners, stains, and patient populations. WMH is itself an imperfect ground truth, subject to orientation, registration, and interobserver variability that AI models inherit.

Implications

WMH-grounded AI is a credible translational route, but routine adoption requires standardized large-format scanning, shared annotation protocols, external validation, and regulatory clearance for autonomous use. We identify field priorities, including cross-institutional WMH datasets, domain-shift mitigation, bias auditing, and reimbursement parity with AI-augmented radiology.

records.title: Present and Future of the Use of Artificial Intelligence in Orthodontics.

content.title: Present and Future of the Use of Artificial Intelligence in Orthodontics.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has penetrated many aspects of orthodontic clinical practice over the past decade. This narrative review aims to highlight all the areas where AI has already entered clinical routine and how it can further improve orthodontic practice in the future. AI is present in diagnostic procedures, facilitating record keeping and supporting the study of patient radiographic and photographic image characteristics. It also underpins the creation and analysis of digital impressions. AI has also become part of patient communication processes, helping to share treatment decisions and facilitating treatment monitoring. Technology and the availability of clinical data also enable the use of AI in diagnostic processes. Currently, clinicians must evaluate AI-provided clinical suggestions before accepting them, as is the case with clear aligner treatments, for example. Research on AI in dentistry, reported in this article, promises to increase the precision of diagnostic measurements and facilitate clinicians' treatment decisions.

records.title: Systematic Review of Algal Toxins in Seals and Sea Lions: Could Unexplained Caspian Seal Mortalities Be Related to Harmful Algae?

content.title: Systematic Review of Algal Toxins in Seals and Sea Lions: Could Unexplained Caspian Seal Mortalities Be Related to Harmful Algae?
content.abstract: Harmful algal blooms (HABs) produce potent neurotoxins, such as domoic acid (DA) and saxitoxin (STX), which negatively impact marine mammal health. To contextualize these threats within specific regional ecosystems, we conducted a comprehensive meta-analysis of algal toxin concentrations in stranded and non-stranded seals and sea lions reported between 1990 and 2025. Following a systematic screening of 2377 records, 15 studies met the criteria for inclusion in our systematic review and quantitative analysis. Both toxins displayed substantial variability among studies. Notably, the concentrations of DA found in feces were markedly higher than in other matrices, and feces appears to be a high-yield matrix for detecting recent exposure. Urine and serum showed moderate DA levels, while fetal fluids were among the lowest. Geographically, most studies originated from California and the Alaskan Arctic. Multi-matrix monitoring of algal toxins is required in remote or logistically challenging regions. We propose that exposure to algal and cyanobacterial neurotoxins is a testable contributor to recurrent, unexplained mass mortality events among Caspian seals (Pusa caspica) and that targeted toxicological screening within the Caspian Sea ecosystem is urgently needed.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence in Gastrointestinal Endoscopy and Hemostatic Decision-Making: Current Evidence, Clinical Implications and Implementation Barriers.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence in Gastrointestinal Endoscopy and Hemostatic Decision-Making: Current Evidence, Clinical Implications and Implementation Barriers.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly transforming gastrointestinal endoscopy by supporting lesion detection, lesion characterization, quality assessment, and clinical risk prediction. Hemostatic decision-making represents a particularly complex field for AI integration, as therapeutic decisions are often made rapidly in the presence of active bleeding, impaired visualization, unstable patients, and variable lesion accessibility. This review critically examines the current evidence for AI-assisted decision-making in gastrointestinal endoscopy and endoscopic hemostasis, with emphasis on gastrointestinal bleeding, prediction of hemostatic therapy requirements, bleeding-risk stratification, rebleeding prediction, transfusion support, and post-procedural monitoring. Available studies suggest that machine learning and deep learning models may outperform conventional scoring systems in selected retrospective or validation cohorts, improve recognition of high-risk lesions, support less experienced endoscopists, and contribute to more individualized management of non-variceal bleeding, variceal bleeding, and capsule endoscopy findings. However, prospective interventional evidence remains sparse, and most available models are limited by retrospective design, single-center datasets, incomplete external validation, black-box decision-making, heterogeneous reporting, workflow barriers, and uncertain cost-effectiveness. AI should therefore be regarded as an adjunctive decision-support tool rather than an autonomous replacement for clinical judgment. Its future value will depend on prospective multicenter validation, explainability, real-time usability, regulatory clarity, post-deployment surveillance, and evidence of improved patient-centered outcomes before widespread implementation in emergency endoscopy practice.

records.title: Methodologies for generating and evaluating clinical and performance evidence for high-risk and innovative medical devices and <i>in vitro</i> diagnostics: a scoping review.

content.title: Methodologies for generating and evaluating clinical and performance evidence for high-risk and innovative medical devices and <i>in vitro</i> diagnostics: a scoping review.
content.abstract:
Introduction

High-risk and innovative medical devices (MDs) and in vitro diagnostic devices (IVDs) in the European Union are subject to increasingly stringent and evolving regulatory requirements. This scoping review maps methodological approaches to evidence generation across their life cycle.

Methods

A comprehensive and systematic search of major bibliographic databases and grey literature sources was conducted (January 2025, updated November 2025). Studies were selected through dual independent screening using predefined inclusion criteria. Data were extracted using a structured approach and supported by AI-assisted thematic analysis. Findings were synthesized narratively to map methodological approaches to evidence generation and evaluation.

Results

A total of 15,679 records were identified, with 14,259 remaining after duplicate removal and 859 full texts assessed for eligibility. Of these, 90 studies met the inclusion criteria. In addition, records identified through other methods were screened, with 75 progressing to full-text assessment; of these, 8 were included. Evidence generation for high-risk and innovative MDs and IVDs requires an integrated, life-cycle approach combining multiple study designs. While randomized controlled trials remain important, observational studies, real-world evidence, registries, and post-market surveillance are essential for assessing long-term safety and effectiveness. However, current practices show substantial variability, methodological limitations, and regulatory inconsistencies.

Conclusions

An integrated lifecycle approach is needed for robust evaluation of high-risk and innovative MDs and IVDs. Strengthening methodological standards, improving the quality of real-world data, and enhancing regulatory harmonization are essential.

Systematic review registration

Open Science Framework (OSF), doi: 10.17605/OSF.IO/XNBSP.

records.title: Large Language Models in Adverse Drug Reaction Detection and Pharmacovigilance: A Systematic Review of Current Applications, Challenges, and Future Directions.

content.title: Large Language Models in Adverse Drug Reaction Detection and Pharmacovigilance: A Systematic Review of Current Applications, Challenges, and Future Directions.
content.abstract: Background/Objectives: Pharmacovigilance workflows rely heavily on unstructured text across diverse sources. Here, we systematically reviewed how large language models (LLMs) are being explored as support tools for adverse drug reaction (ADR) detection, extraction, triage, and documentation, highlighting their potential for precision medicine and big data-enabled safety monitoring. Methods: Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 guidelines, we systematically searched PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science for studies published between January 2022 and March 2026. Ultimately, 83 empirical studies satisfied the inclusion criteria. A narrative synthesis was conducted to address methodological heterogeneity across these studies. Results: LLM applications were concentrated in constrained information-extraction and classification tasks, including signal evaluation, clinical-note extraction, social media surveillance, and literature screening. Quantitative performance varied substantially by system design: error-correction prompting yielded an F1-score of 0.921 for ADR named entity recognition, whereas retrieval-augmented generation improved data-retrieval accuracy from 8.3% to 78.3%. Most studies were retrospective, benchmark-based, or proof-of-concept evaluations. Across 581 paired pre-consensus domain judgements, observed inter-rater agreement was 90.4% and Cohen's κ was 0.837 (95% CI 0.772-0.895). Hallucination, low specificity, prompt sensitivity, narrow datasets, and weak external validation remained common limitations. Conclusions: Current evidence supports supervised, task-specific applications of LLMs for extraction, triage, retrieval, and documentation rather than autonomous pharmacovigilance decision-making. Prospective evaluation, external validation, transparent reporting, and accountable human oversight are required before high-stakes clinical or regulatory deployment.

records.title: Evaluating combined acupuncture and antiresorptive therapy in Chinese women with postmenopausal osteoporosis: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.

content.title: Evaluating combined acupuncture and antiresorptive therapy in Chinese women with postmenopausal osteoporosis: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Postmenopausal osteoporosis (PMOP) is a common metabolic disorder in middle-aged and older women, leading to fractures, disability, and increased mortality. Current treatments include bisphosphonates (BPs), calcitonin (CT), vitamin D (VD), and acupuncture (Acu), often used in combination, but comparative evidence on different combined strategies remain limited.

Objective

To systematically compare the efficacy and safety of acupuncture combined with various medications for PMOP, supporting evidence-based clinical decisions.

Methods

We searched eight databases from inception to April 11, 2026 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating acupuncture plus pharmacotherapy for PMOP. Primary outcomes included lumbar spine (LS) and femoral neck (FN) bone mineral density (BMD), clinical efficacy, Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) syndrome scores, and Visual Analog Scale (VAS) pain scores. Secondary outcomes were procollagen type I N-terminal propeptide (PINP), C-terminal telopeptide (CTX), estradiol (E2), alkaline phosphatase (ALP), and osteocalcin (OCN). A Bayesian network meta-analysis was performed, ranking treatments by surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA).

Results

We included 112 RCTs (9, 908 patients, 83 treatment strategies). For LS-BMD, Calcitriol (Cal)_Electroacupuncture (ElecAcu) ranked highest. For FN-BMD, CT_VD_Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM)_Fire dragon moxibustion (FDMox) (without BP) and CT_VD_BP_TCM_Acu (with BP) were best. TCM_Acu showed the best clinical efficacy. For TCM syndrome total score, CT_VD_ Du-moxibustion (DuMox) ranked lowest. For low back pain, TCM_Acu (without BP) and CT_VD_BP_Acu_Moxibustion (Mox) (with BP) were best. CT_VD_BP_Acu_Point Application Therapy (Pat) ranked lowest for VAS. CT_VD_BP_Acupoint injection (AcuInj) produced the lowest PINP, CT_VD_TCM_Acu the lowest CTX, and CT_VD_BP_TCM_Acupoint catgut embedding (ACE) the highest E2. For ALP, CT_VD_BP_Acu ranked lowest with BP, and CT_VD_Mox highest without BP. For OCN, CT_VD_Mox ranked highest without BP, and CT_VD_BP_TCM_Acu_Mox highest with BP.

Conclusion

Acupuncture combined with pharmacotherapy offers differential benefits across efficacy outcomes in PMOP. However, fracture data were nearly absent (only one trial reported two hip fractures) and follow-up was short (≤12 months), limiting any inference on fracture prevention. Treatment selection should be individualized based on therapeutic priorities and patient characteristics, supporting personalized integrative management strategies.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420251233374.

records.title: A comprehensive study of skin lesion segmentation and classification using deep learning techniques.

content.title: A comprehensive study of skin lesion segmentation and classification using deep learning techniques.
content.abstract: Deep learning has become an important computational approach in dermatology because it enables automated segmentation and classification of skin lesions. Manual dermoscopic analysis is time-consuming and depends on specialist expertise, with potential inter-observer variability. There is a need to develop reliable computer-aided diagnostic tools. This structured narrative review covers journal papers published mainly from 2018 to 2026 on skin lesion analysis with focus on image preprocessing, benchmark datasets, conventional machine learning approaches, convolutional neural networks, U-Net architectures, transfer learning approaches, Vision Transformers, attention-based models, ensemble solutions, and hybrid segmentation-classification systems. Building on present reviews covering individual tasks as well as broader segmentation-classification pipelines, the present work provides a critical development-to-deployment analysis connecting dataset characteristics, preprocessing, segmentation, classification, evaluation, explainability, robustness, fairness, computational requirements, and clinical applicability. The paper describes widely used evaluation metrics and explains why results obtained across different datasets, partitions, and experimental setups should not be directly compared. Major open problems include class imbalance, data bias, domain shift, limited representation of diverse skin tones, inadequate external validation, computational requirements, and limited explainability of efficient models. Emerging trends such as self-supervised learning, Transformers, foundation models, explainable AI, federated learning, and multi-modal clinical data are reviewed as well. The review offers practical advice to researchers and clinicians on how to approach the preprocessing, segmentation, classification, and evaluation of skin lesions and highlights priorities in developing clinically reliable skin lesion analysis systems.

records.title: Traditional Chinese mind-body practices and depressive symptoms in university students: a multilevel dose-response meta-analysis.

content.title: Traditional Chinese mind-body practices and depressive symptoms in university students: a multilevel dose-response meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Objective

Numerous meta-analyses have evaluated Tai Chi, Qigong and related traditional Chinese mind-body practices (TCMBPs) for depressive symptoms across broader populations; however, to our knowledge, no previous meta-analysis has focused specifically on university students. We therefore aimed to estimate the average effect of TCMBPs on depressive symptoms in this population using a three-level model that explicitly accounts for dependent effect sizes, and to explore nonlinear dose-response patterns and Bayesian cumulative exposure.

Methods

PubMed, Web of Science, PsycINFO, the Cochrane Library and CNKI were searched from inception to 29 December 2025 for randomized controlled trials. Effect sizes were synthesized with a three-level random-effects model. Heterogeneity, small-study effects and influential estimates were examined using prespecified diagnostics, sensitivity analyses and cluster-robust variance estimation. Subgroup, meta-regression and Bayesian dose-response analyses were treated as exploratory.

Results

Fifteen randomized controlled trials met the eligibility criteria. After influence diagnostics, the pooled estimate indicated lower depressive-symptom scores after traditional Chinese mind-body practice (SMD = -0.56, 95% CI - 0.84 to -0.27; p < 0.001), although heterogeneity was substantial and the certainty of evidence was moderate. The estimate was similar with cluster-robust variance estimation. Subgroup patterns differed by practice, comparator and participant characteristics, but most contrasts were supported by few studies. Bayesian models placed the lowest fitted effect near a cumulative dose of 33.7 h; this estimate arose from sparse and uneven exposure data and should not be interpreted as a prescriptive optimum.

Conclusion

Traditional Chinese mind-body practices were associated with a moderate average reduction in depressive symptoms and may be feasible complements to university mental-health programs. Because the evidence was heterogeneous, concentrated in China and of moderate certainty, the findings do not establish equivalent benefits across practices or a recommended dose. Larger, better-reported randomized trials are needed.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251275476, identifier PROSPERO (CRD420251275476).

records.title: Next-Generation Target Discovery in ESKAPE Pathogens: An AI-Driven Framework from Omics-Based to Systems-Level Modeling and Clinical Translation.

content.title: Next-Generation Target Discovery in ESKAPE Pathogens: An AI-Driven Framework from Omics-Based to Systems-Level Modeling and Clinical Translation.
content.abstract: Background: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) among ESKAPE pathogens-Enterococcus faecium, Staphylococcus aureus, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Acinetobacter baumannii, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Enterobacter spp.-represents a major global health threat and accounts for a substantial proportion of healthcare-associated infections. Their genomic plasticity and adaptive regulatory responses facilitate the rapid emergence and dissemination of resistance and virulence determinants. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a powerful approach for analyzing large-scale biological datasets and identifying molecular signatures associated with antimicrobial resistance and pathogenicity. Objectives: This review examines AI-driven frameworks for predictive target discovery in ESKAPE pathogens, focusing on approaches that leverage genomic and transcriptomic data and extend toward the integration of additional omics layers within network-based and systems-level modeling frameworks. We discuss how AI methods are evolving beyond phenotypic prediction toward more biologically interpretable inference for prioritizing resistance mechanisms, virulence determinants, and candidate antimicrobial targets. Conclusions and Future Directions: Current AI applications exploit genomic, transcriptomic, and network-level data to prioritize resistance and virulence determinants and to support antimicrobial discovery, including small molecules and antimicrobial peptides. However, integrative multi-layer modeling and comprehensive experimental validation remain limited. Future advances will depend on improved integration of complementary biological data, enhanced model interpretability, and robust translational validation frameworks to enable clinically actionable AI-guided novel pathogen-targeted next-generation diagnostics, therapeutic and stewardship strategies against ESKAPE pathogens.

records.title: Psychedelics in neurosurgery: Potential utility in prevention, perioperative care, pain management, and neurorehabilitation.

content.title: Psychedelics in neurosurgery: Potential utility in prevention, perioperative care, pain management, and neurorehabilitation.
content.abstract:
Background

Neurosurgical patients carry a high and frequently undertreated burden of psychological suffering, acute and chronic pain, and neurological deficits amenable to recovery. The resurgence of psychedelic research has produced relevant evidence in adjacent fields, but its applicability to neurosurgery has not been systematized. This review synthesizes that evidence across prevention, perioperative care, pain management, and neurorehabilitation, and delineates the safety considerations specific to neurosurgery.

Methods

Narrative review structured around a population, intervention, comparator, outcome, and time question, covering 2020-2026. The classic serotonergic psychedelics (psilocybin, lysergic acid diethylamide [LSD], N,N-dimethyltryptamine, ayahuasca, 5-methoxy-N,N-dimethyltryptamine, and mescaline), the iboga alkaloid ibogaine, the entactogen 3,4-methylenedioxymethamphetamine, and the dissociatives ketamine and esketamine were examined. Randomized controlled trials, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and high-quality mechanistic studies were prioritized.

Results

No trial has administered these agents in neurosurgical cohorts, so all evidence is indirect. Psilocybin- assisted therapy produces substantial, durable reductions in cancer-related depression, anxiety, and existential distress. LSD is anxiolytic; parenteral tryptamines act rapidly in depression; ibogaine improved disability, post- traumatic stress, and cognition after traumatic brain injury but carries arrhythmia risk. Perioperative ketamine and esketamine show antidepressant and opioid-sparing effects. Classic psychedelics promote neuroplasticity and are neuroprotective in preclinical models.

Conclusion

A biologically plausible basis exists for exploring these agents in neurosurgery, but direct evidence is absent and translation is constrained by the seizure threshold, hemodynamic and cerebrovascular effects, perioperative serotonergic interactions, and the need for structured psychological support. Perioperative esketamine and psilocybin for neuro-oncological distress are the most feasible starting points. Purpose-designed neurosurgical trials are required.

records.title: AI-Enabled Personalization of Semaglutide Therapy in Type 2 Diabetes: Systematic Review With an Integration Framework.

content.title: AI-Enabled Personalization of Semaglutide Therapy in Type 2 Diabetes: Systematic Review With an Integration Framework.
content.abstract:
Background

Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2D) is a rapidly growing global health concern requiring innovative treatment methods. Ozempic (semaglutide), a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist, has proven consistent effectiveness in lowering blood glucose levels, supporting weight loss, and minimizing cardiovascular complications. In parallel, artificial intelligence (AI) elevates diabetes care yet complements these efforts by converting raw data from wearable devices, electronic health records, and medical imaging into practical insights for efficient, tailored, and customized treatment plans.

Objective

The objective of this systematic review is to examine current evidence of AI-driven methods to optimize Ozempic-based T2D therapy.

Methods

A total of 18 peer-reviewed articles were identified, revealing four dominant thematic clusters: (1) patient stratification and risk prediction, (2) AI-enhanced imaging for body composition changes, (3) cardiovascular and metabolic risk assessment, and (4) personalized AI-driven dosage.

Results

Across multiple metrics, such as glycated hemoglobin reduction, weight loss, cardiovascular benefits, and adverse event mitigation, AI-based approaches outperformed standard fixed-dose regimens. A theoretical framework is proposed for AI-Ozempic integration, with continuous data collection, AI processing, clinical decision support, real-time support, and real-time feedback and modeling iteration refinement cycles.

Conclusions

Significant gaps remain a persistent challenge, including the need for large-scale randomized controlled trials, longer follow-up periods, explainable AI models, regulatory validation, and practical strategies for routine clinical implementation. The findings emphasize the AI's potential to transform semaglutide therapy while delineating important paths for future research.

records.title: Machine Learning for the Interpretation of Serum Protein and Immunofixation Electrophoresis in Multiple Myeloma: A Scoping Review.

content.title: Machine Learning for the Interpretation of Serum Protein and Immunofixation Electrophoresis in Multiple Myeloma: A Scoping Review.
content.abstract: Background: Serum protein electrophoresis (SPE) and immunofixation electrophoresis (IFE) are essential in diagnosing multiple myeloma (MM). Machine learning (ML) methods have emerged as a potential approach to the automation process of electrophoresis interpretation to improve diagnostic efficiency and improve turnaround time. This scoping review mapped current applications of ML in the diagnosis and classification of MM, with emphasis on automated SPE and IFE interpretation. Methods: PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus databases were searched following PRISMA-ScR guidance. Articles published between January 2015 and April 2025 applying ML to MM diagnosis were included, and findings were synthesised descriptively and thematically. Results: Thirteen studies were included, identifying two dominant application domains: ML-based analysis of IFE images and SPE patterns. Deep learning models, particularly convolutional neural networks, achieved expert-level performance in IFE analysis, with peak accuracies reaching 99.82% and F1-scores frequently exceeding 0.90. For SPE interpretation, both deep learning and classical tree-based models demonstrated robust diagnostic yields, achieving Areas Under the Curve (AUC) between 0.90 and 0.99 and overall accuracies ranging from 82.8% to 99.1%. Notably, top-performing models recorded F1-scores up to 0.98, and in some instances, they surpassed the precision of human expert panels. Conclusions: Explainable AI methods were increasingly incorporated, though external validation, multimodal integration, explainability, and real-world deployment were limited. ML demonstrates potential to augment SPE and IFE interpretation in MM diagnostics. Future work should focus on multicentre validation, explainability, and clinical integration to support safe implementation.

records.title: Green toxicology only becomes beautiful through AI.

content.title: Green toxicology only becomes beautiful through AI.
content.abstract: Green Toxicology extends the principles of Green Chemistry by embedding toxicological foresight into chemical design, with the aim of preventing hazards before substances reach markets or the environment. Its conceptual pillars-prevention, precaution, life-cycle thinking, and avoidance of regrettable substitutions-align closely with sustainability agendas such as the European Green Deal and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. Despite its promise, Green Toxicology has remained largely aspirational, limited by fragmented data, slow regulatory uptake, and reliance on new approach methodologies (NAMs) that still face validation and acceptance hurdles. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers a transformative solution by integrating heterogeneous datasets, enhancing predictive accuracy, and enabling probabilistic risk assessment. Deep learning, natural language processing, and explainable AI can mine legacy studies, link adverse outcome pathways, and design safer chemistries proactively. Coupled with microphysiological systems and omics, AI makes Green Toxicology predictive, human-relevant, and scalable. Together, they form a practical framework for guiding chemical innovation toward sustainability, reconciling industrial productivity with ecological integrity and public health protection.

records.title: Associations between pretreatment systemic immune-inflammation index and tumor-specific prognosis in breast and gynecological cancers: an updated systematic review, meta-analysis, and certainty-of-evidence assessment.

content.title: Associations between pretreatment systemic immune-inflammation index and tumor-specific prognosis in breast and gynecological cancers: an updated systematic review, meta-analysis, and certainty-of-evidence assessment.
content.abstract:
Introduction

Recent meta-analyses have assessed the prognostic value of the systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) in individual breast or gynecological cancers, but pooling these biologically distinct malignancies into one analysis has limited validity. Substantial differences in disease stage, treatment, SII thresholds, covariate adjustment, and outcome definitions add further uncertainty. This revised study therefore used a tumor-specific framework without assuming a common effect across female malignancies.

Methods

Four databases were searched through July 22, 2023, with structured top-up search and citation tracking through August 5, 2026. Current disease-specific meta-analyses served as quantitative sources when more robust than the original evidence; post-review primary studies were synthesized narratively to avoid double counting. Breast, cervical, ovarian, endometrial, and vulvar cancers were evaluated separately, with assessment of cohort overlap, residual confounding, sparse endpoints, threshold validity, heterogeneity, and certainty of evidence. No overall pooled estimate was calculated.

Results

The updated evidence map used current quantitative sources comprising 28 breast cancer studies (17,291 participants), 16 cervical cancer studies(2,840 participants), 10 ovarian cancer studies representing 11 cohorts (2,852 participants), and 8 endometrial cancer studies(2,315 participants). Targeted post-review updates included one additional cervical cancer cohort (470 participants), three later endometrial cancer reports, and three vulvar cancer reports(295 participants); these narrative updates were not added to the source-review denominators. Elevated SII was associated with poorer overall survival(OS), disease-free survival(DFS), and distant metastasis-free survival (DMFS) in breast cancer; poorer OS and progression-free survival (PFS) in cervical cancer; poorer OS and DFS in ovarian cancer; and poorer OS and PFS in endometrial cancer. The pathologic complete response (pCR) in breast cancer was not significantly associated with SII. The findings related to DMFS and vulvar cancer were statistically sparse. Substantial or very high heterogeneity persisted in several analyses, and all principal outcomes were rated as very-low-certainty evidence.

Conclusions

Elevated pretreatment SII was associated with adverse outcomes in several tumor-specific settings, but the magnitude and transportability of associations remain uncertain. Evidence cannot establish a universal threshold, confirm incremental prognostic value beyond established clinical factors, or support sufficient net benefit for treatment decisions. SII should therefore serve as an adjunct rather than a stand-alone clinical tool.Systematic review registration:https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/, identifier CRD 42023444334.

records.title: Novel Approaches to the Management of Myelodysplastic Syndromes: The Roles of Artificial Intelligence and Oxidative Stress Biomarkers.

content.title: Novel Approaches to the Management of Myelodysplastic Syndromes: The Roles of Artificial Intelligence and Oxidative Stress Biomarkers.
content.abstract: Objectives: Myelodysplastic syndromes (MDSs) are a heterogeneous group of clonal hematopoietic disorders characterized by ineffective hematopoiesis, genomic instability, and a high risk of progression to acute myeloid leukemia. Oxidative stress (OS) has emerged as a central factor in MDS pathophysiology, contributing to DNA damage, altered cellular signaling, and disease progression. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) offer a transformative approach for integrating multidimensional datasets including oxidative stress markers, hematologic parameters, and molecular profiles to enhance diagnosis, prognostication, and therapeutic monitoring in MDS. Methods: A comprehensive literature search was conducted in PubMed and Scopus, using the keywords "OS biomarkers," "AI," and "MDS''. Results: Modified redox biomarkers can be correlated with oxidative imbalance and disease progression. ML models such as neural networks, decision trees, and support vector machines effectively capture complex relationships among redox biomarkers, enhancing risk stratification and prediction of treatment response. AI-driven proteomic analyses further revealed OS-related protein signatures linked to MDS pathophysiology. Overall, AI and ML enable the transformation of multidimensional OS data into clinically actionable tools for personalized management in MDS. Conclusions: Integrating biomarker research with AI-based analytics holds promise for advancing personalized diagnostics, prognostication, and therapeutic strategies in MDS, paving the way toward precision medicine.

records.title: Artificial intelligence revolution in toxicology: Clinical precision, global equity, and the 2030 roadmap.

content.title: Artificial intelligence revolution in toxicology: Clinical precision, global equity, and the 2030 roadmap.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming toxicology by enabling faster, more accurate, and more equitable approaches to diagnosis, treatment, research, and education. This review synthesizes recent advances in AI applications across clinical toxicology, predictive modeling, pharmacovigilance, and training, highlighting innovations such as deep learning for diagnostic stratification, reinforcement learning for personalized antidote dosing, and generative AI for virtual patient simulations. While these technologies demonstrate substantial promise, their clinical and regulatory adoption remains constrained by algorithmic bias, limited model interpretability, validation challenges specific to feature importance accuracy, and persistent global digital inequities. Critical limitations include the distinction between target prediction accuracy and feature importance accuracy in supervised models, where high predictive performance does not guarantee mechanistic reliability. Moreover, the potential for AI-generated misinformation and the need for continuous human oversight in clinical contexts warrant careful consideration. To guide responsible integration, the "ToxAI Pact" is proposed, a 2030 roadmap emphasizing harmonized validation standards, robust feature importance validation protocols, watermarking of generative outputs, and infrastructure investment for low-resource settings. By embedding fairness, explainability, and robust governance, AI can evolve from experimental tools into foundational infrastructure for safer, more inclusive toxicology worldwide.

records.title: Effects of different recovery and regeneration modalities on delayed-onset muscle soreness and post-exercise muscle damage markers: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.

content.title: Effects of different recovery and regeneration modalities on delayed-onset muscle soreness and post-exercise muscle damage markers: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Objective

This study employed a systematic review and Bayesian network meta-analysis to compare the effects of multiple post-exercise interventions during the early recovery period, examine whether these effects varied across recovery time points, and provide evidence to inform the selection of post-exercise recovery strategies.

Methods

PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were systematically searched, and randomized controlled trials, including parallel-group and crossover designs, were included. A Bayesian random-effects network meta-analysis was used to estimate mean differences (MDs) and 95% credible intervals (CrIs). The revised Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials (RoB 2) and the Confidence in Network Meta-Analysis (CINeMA) framework were used to assess risk of bias and confidence in the evidence, respectively. Sensitivity analyses and exploratory univariable network meta-regression analyses were also performed.

Results

A total of 35 studies were included in this review. For delayed-onset muscle soreness (DOMS), whole-body cryotherapy (WBC) and photobiomodulation/phototherapy-related interventions (PHO) showed relatively large reductions in soreness at both 24 and 48 h after exercise. Compared with the combined control/placebo condition (CON/PBO), the effect estimates for WBC were MD = -38.92 (95% CrI: -69.08 to -9.15) at 24 h and MD = -40.03 (95% CrI: -67.74 to -12.44) at 48 h. The corresponding estimates for PHO were MD = -18.20 (95% CrI: -32.91 to -3.72) and MD = -19.46 (95% CrI: -33.55 to -5.99), respectively. For creatine kinase (CK), low-level laser therapy (LLLT) and PHO were associated with lower CK levels at both 24 and 48 h, with the largest estimated effect for LLLT at 48 h (MD = -499.96, 95% CrI: -831.59 to -203.59). For interleukin-6 (IL-6), CWI showed favorable estimates at both 24 and 48 h, although the evidence base was limited and the network was sparse.

Conclusion

WBC and PHO showed relatively consistent favorable effects on DOMS at 24 and 48 h, whereas LLLT and PHO showed relatively consistent associations with lower CK levels. The IL-6 findings should be interpreted as exploratory because of the limited evidence base. Selection of post-exercise recovery strategies should consider the target outcome, recovery time window, evidence certainty, and network structure.

records.title: Dumbbell Bench Press and Dumbbell Fly Elicit Similar Pectoralis Major Muscle Hypertrophy in Recreationally Trained Men.
records.publisher: Journal of strength and conditioning research

content.title: Dumbbell Bench Press and Dumbbell Fly Elicit Similar Pectoralis Major Muscle Hypertrophy in Recreationally Trained Men.
content.abstract:
Abstract

Dell'Avanzi, FG, Enes, A, Alves-Marques, F, Costa-Rodrigues, J, Bello, G, Seima, G, Nass, G, Moreira, NF, Santana, C, Mohan, AE, Piñero, A, Schoenfeld, BJ, and Souza-Junior, TP. Dumbbell bench press and dumbbell fly elicit similar pectoralis major muscle hypertrophy in recreationally trained men. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-Exercise selection is one of the main resistance training (RT) variables for eliciting inhomogeneous muscle growth. Whether exercises that differ in resistance moment arm elicit whole- and nonuniform hypertrophy of the pectoralis major remains unclear. This study investigated the effects of the dumbbell bench press (DBP) and dumbbell fly (DFLY) on pectoralis major muscle thickness (MT). Twenty-six young healthy men (RT experience 3.3 ± 3.1 years) were allocated to DBP or DFLY groups, training twice a week over a 10-week period. The weekly set number was individualized according to subjects' previous RT pectoralis major volume. Pectoralis major MT was assessed by ultrasound imaging at medial (30%), intermediate (50%), and lateral (70%) sites at baseline and postintervention. Our mixed-model analysis indicated a main effect for time (p < 0.05) but no time-by-group interaction for the medial site (p = 0.500), intermediate site (p = 0.864), lateral site (p = 0.720), and the sum of the MT across sites (p = 0.985). Therefore, both exercises elicited similar general and regional hypertrophy on pectoralis major MT in recreationally trained individuals. Coaches and practitioners can select DBP or DFLY when targeting pectoralis major muscle development in recreationally trained men based on personal preference and goals within the RT program.

records.title: Is plant-based protein supplementation as effective as whey protein? A systematic review and meta-analysis in untrained adults undergoing resistance training.
records.publisher: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition

content.title: Is plant-based protein supplementation as effective as whey protein? A systematic review and meta-analysis in untrained adults undergoing resistance training.
content.abstract:
Background

Dietary protein supplements are commonly consumed to support increases in lean body mass among healthy adults engaged in resistance training (RT). Although whey protein has been extensively investigated, plant-based protein supplements have emerged as a viable alternative for individuals who avoid animal-derived products.

Methods

The present study aims to evaluate, through a systematic review and meta-analysis, the effects of plant-based versus whey protein supplementation on body composition in untrained adults (18-59 years) undergoing RT, using Dual-Energy X-Ray Absorptiometry (DEXA). The systematic review was conducted according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 checklist and was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251145410). Searches were conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect, identifying 5 studies that met the inclusion criteria for qualitative synthesis and meta-analysis.

Results

When combined with RT, both plant-based and whey protein supplementation were associated with improvements in lean body mass (LBM) and body fat mass (BFM), with no significant between-group differences observed.

Conclusions

Thus, soy- and pea-based protein supplements may support favorable body composition changes in adults initiating RT and could be considered practical nutritional options for individuals seeking alternatives to whey protein. Regarding chia-based protein, the available evidence is currently limited to a single study that did not demonstrate significant changes in lean body mass; therefore, firm conclusions regarding its efficacy cannot be drawn at this time.

records.title: How Often Should Volume Increase? Effects of Different Volume-Progression Frequencies on Strength and Hypertrophy Adaptations in Women.
records.publisher: Journal of strength and conditioning research

content.title: How Often Should Volume Increase? Effects of Different Volume-Progression Frequencies on Strength and Hypertrophy Adaptations in Women.
content.abstract:
Abstract

Enes, A, Macedo, ACG, Nass, G, Costa-Rodrigues, J, Alves-Marques, F, Santana, C, Dell'Avanzi, FG, Rodrigues, BG, Alves, RC, De Souza, EO, and Souza-Junior, TP. How often should volume increase? Effects of different volume-progression frequencies on strength and hypertrophy adaptations in females. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-Resistance training (RT) volume is an important programming variable for strength and hypertrophy. However, how frequently RT volume should be progressed remains unclear. Thus, we investigated the effects of progressively increasing RT volume by 2 weekly sets targeting the quadriceps femoris every 2 weeks (2 W) or every 4 weeks (4 W) over a 12-week period in recreationally trained women. Using a within-subject design and accounting for previous RT volume, 21 subjects (age 23.3 ± 3.9 years; RT experience 1.1 ± 0.7 years) had their limbs assigned to one of the 2 conditions: 2 weeks (2 W) or 4 weeks (4 W). 45° leg-press 1-repetition maximum (1RM) and the sum of muscle thickness (∑MT) of the proximal (30%), middle (50%), and distal (70%) portions of the lateral thigh were assessed at baseline and after 12 weeks. Our mixed-model analysis indicated a main effect of time for 1RM (p < 0.0001), with no difference between the 2 and 4 W conditions (p = 0.317). Similarly, regarding the ∑MT, the analysis indicated a main effect of time (p < 0.001), with no difference between the conditions (p = 0.616). Within the relatively high training volumes examined, progressing the RT volume by 2 weekly sets every 2 or 4 weeks did not elicit detectable differences in strength and hypertrophy adaptations over 12 weeks in recreationally trained women.

records.title: Lower-Body Strength and Hypertrophy Adaptations in Response to Concurrent Training in Trained Young Males.
records.publisher: Journal of strength and conditioning research

content.title: Lower-Body Strength and Hypertrophy Adaptations in Response to Concurrent Training in Trained Young Males.
content.abstract:
Abstract

Gomes, M, Costa, M, Pezarat-Correia, P, and Mendonca, GV. Lower-body strength and hypertrophy adaptations in response to concurrent training in trained young males. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-This study examined the interference effect of concurrent training (CT) on maximal and explosive strength and muscle morphology in trained young males. Thirty subjects were randomly assigned to endurance training (E), resistance training (R), or CT for 11 weeks. The intervention comprised 2 mesocycles: weeks 1-5 emphasizing maximal strength, and weeks 6-11 targeting explosive strength. Assessments were conducted at baseline, mid-training, and post-training, and included leg-press maximal voluntary isometric contraction (MVIC), rate of force development (RFD), countermovement jump kinetics, and vastus lateralis cross-sectional area and pennation angle. Maximal voluntary isometric contraction increased only in the R group (18.4 ± 10.2%, p = 0.015). Peak RFD improved in both R (31.8 ± 23.2%) and CT (23.1 ± 27.9%), although with distinct time courses: R improved progressively across both mesocycles, whereas CT improved only during the second. Early-phase RFD (0-50 ms) increased in the R group from mid-training onward, whereas the CT group improved only from mid- to post-training (38.3 ± 40.4%, p = 0.021), accompanied by greater quadriceps electromyographic activity (p < 0.05). No changes in RFD were observed in E during training. Countermovement jump positive impulse improved in both R (12.7 ± 9.0%) and CT (8.8 ± 8.3%, p < 0.05), with no evidence of interference in jump-related explosive performance. Cross-sectional area increased in both R (17.0 ± 13.0%) and CT (8.8 ± 9.4%, p < 0.05). Pennation angle increased in CT (10.1 ± 12.9%) and R (18.6 ± 15.1%). These findings indicate that, although CT may limit MVIC development and delay early-phase RFD adaptations, it does not hinder explosive performance when resistance training is oriented toward rapid-strength development. Thus, CT can be effectively implemented in trained individuals when resistance training is periodized to emphasize neural-driven explosive or hypertrophy-related adaptations.

records.title: Citrulline Malate Ingestion Enhances Muscular Performance During a Selected Hypertrophy Hack Squat Training Protocol.
records.publisher: Journal of strength and conditioning research

content.title: Citrulline Malate Ingestion Enhances Muscular Performance During a Selected Hypertrophy Hack Squat Training Protocol.
content.abstract:
Abstract

Wax, B, Dorgo, S, Montalvo, S, Lyons, B, and Mayo, JJ. Citrulline malate ingestion enhances muscular performance during a selected hypertrophy hack squat training protocol. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-This study examined potential ergogenic effects of an oral citrulline malate supplement (CM) during lower-body resistance training. Fifteen resistance-trained men completed a randomized, counterbalanced, double-blind crossover design. Subjects ingested 8.0 g CM or placebo 60 minutes before 8 sets of hack squats at 67% one-repetition maximum to failure with 90-second recovery intervals, repeating the protocol with the alternate treatment 1 week later. Blood lactate before and after exercise, rating of perceived exertion after sets 4 and 8, muscle soreness at 24 and 48 hours, and heart rate and blood pressure at rest and 5 and 10 minutes after exercise were assessed. Hack squat repetition numbers were higher overall in the CM condition (condition effect p = 0.0213), and CM increased total repetitions by 10.7 (95% confidence interval 1.4 to 20.0; p = 0.0265; Hedges' g = 0.61) and total workload by 1,064.7 units (95% confidence interval 84.1 to 2045.4; p = 0.0354; Hedges' g = 0.57). Blood lactate increased after exercise but did not differ by condition. Rating of perceived exertion showed no significant condition effect or Holm-adjusted set-specific difference. Citrulline malate was associated with significantly lower muscle soreness overall and at both 24 and 48 hours after exercise. Heart rate and systolic blood pressure showed condition × time interactions, with Holm-adjusted CM vs. placebo differences at 5 minutes after exercise, whereas diastolic blood pressure showed no significant condition effect or Holm-adjusted time-point difference. Acute CM supplementation may improve lower-body resistance training work capacity and reduce perceived soreness without altering lactate accumulation or perceived exertion.

records.title: Comparative Effects of Resistance Training and High-Intensity Interval Training on Body Composition, Metabolic Health, and Functional Strength in Overweight and Obese Adults: A 12-Week Randomized Controlled Trial.
records.publisher: Journal of strength and conditioning research

content.title: Comparative Effects of Resistance Training and High-Intensity Interval Training on Body Composition, Metabolic Health, and Functional Strength in Overweight and Obese Adults: A 12-Week Randomized Controlled Trial.
content.abstract:
Abstract

Petisco-Rodríguez, C, Barroso-Hernández, Á, Bartolomé-Sánchez, I, and Crego, A. Comparative effects of resistance training and high-intensity interval training on body composition, metabolic health, and functional strength in overweight and obese adults: A 12-week randomized controlled trial. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-The aim of this study was to compare the effects of 2 training programs on anthropometric and physiological variables in overweight and obese adults. Ninety subjects (age = 39.9 ± 10.4 years; body mass index (BMI) = 31.0 ± 4.3 kg·m-2) were randomly assigned to a resistance training group (RG; n = 30), a high-intensity interval training (HIIT) group (HG; n = 30), or a nontraining control group (CG; n = 30). Both the RG and HG performed 2 weekly sessions for 12 weeks. The RG completed 8 upper-body and lower-body resistance exercises at 70% of 1 repetition maximum, while the HG performed high-intensity intervals at 80% of the maximum heart rate. A 3 (group: CG, RG, HG) × 2 (time: pre, post) mixed ANOVA revealed significant effects on the BMI, body fat, and fasting glucose. Both training groups showed similar improvements in all measures from preintervention to postintervention. Compared with CG, RG and HG had reduced body fat and BMI, while RG demonstrated greater gains in muscle mass, fasting glucose, and grip strength. Paired t-tests confirmed significant within-group improvements in BMI, body fat, grip strength, and fasting glucose in the RG and HG. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.017 after the Bonferroni correction. These findings suggest that both resistance training and HIIT enhance the body composition of overweight and obese adults. However, resistance training may provide additional benefits in muscular fitness and glycemic control, supporting its role as a practical strategy for improving metabolic health in this population.

records.title: Effectiveness of Pelvic Floor Muscle Training in Women Soccer Players and Its Relationship With Quality of Life and Pelvic Floor Muscle Strength: A Randomized Controlled Pilot Study.
records.publisher: Journal of strength and conditioning research

content.title: Effectiveness of Pelvic Floor Muscle Training in Women Soccer Players and Its Relationship With Quality of Life and Pelvic Floor Muscle Strength: A Randomized Controlled Pilot Study.
content.abstract:
Abstract

Sebastian-Rico, JM, Muñoz-Fernández, MJ, Martínez-Aranda, LM, Calvo-Lluch, Á, and Ortega-Becerra, M. Effectiveness of pelvic floor muscle training in women soccer players and its relationship with quality of life and pelvic floor muscle strength: a randomized controlled pilot study. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-This study investigated the effects of a 6-week pelvic floor muscle training (PFMT) program on muscle strength, function, and the prevalence of related dysfunctions in professional female soccer players using a randomized controlled pilot study design. Twenty nulliparous professional soccer players from the Spanish professional league (2024-2025 season) were randomly assigned to an experimental group (n = 12) or a control group (n = 8). Assessments included anthropometric data, validated questionnaires (International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire-Short Form and Broome Pelvic Muscle Self-Efficacy Scale), clinical interviews, and physical examination using the PERFECT method and manometry. The intervention consisted of a 6-week supervised PFMT program (4 sessions/week, 30 minutes each) progressed through 4 phases: education, proprioception, strengthening, and functional integration. Results showed significant group × time interactions for pelvic floor self-efficacy (Broome Pelvic Muscle Self-Efficacy Scale), with scores in the PFMT group increasing by 48.8 and 59.6% (p < 0.05), representing large between-group effect sizes (d = 0.91-1.26). Pelvic floor muscle performance increased by 122.4% in the intervention group (d = 1.25), whereas no meaningful changes were observed in the control group. No adverse events were reported. In conclusion, a 6-week supervised PFMT program is an effective and safe intervention for professional female soccer players, significantly improving muscle function and self-efficacy. These findings support the integration of PFMT for both therapeutic and preventive purposes in elite, high-impact sports environments.

records.title: Performance and Physiological Responses to Strength Training Programs in Elite Judo Athletes.
records.publisher: Journal of strength and conditioning research

content.title: Performance and Physiological Responses to Strength Training Programs in Elite Judo Athletes.
content.abstract:
Abstract

Campos, BT, Rodrigues, JGdS, Cal Abad, CC, Bachi, ALL, dos Santos, CMM, Tritto, AC, Kons, RL, Penna, EM, and Prado, LS. Performance and physiological responses to strength training programs in elite judo athletes. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-This study compared the effects of 2 short-term strength training models, block planning (BP) and undulating planning (UP), on performance, physiological, and perceptual responses in elite judo athletes. We hypothesized that BP would induce greater physiological strain due to the concentration of training stimuli. Eighteen judokas (14 men and 4 women) were randomly assigned to BP (n = 9) or UP (n = 9) for 4 weeks, performing 6 weekly strength sessions alongside technical-tactical training. Performance outcomes included countermovement jump (CMJ), muscle power (back squat and bent-over row), and the Special Judo Fitness Test (SJFT). Monitoring variables included internal load, heart rate variability (HRV), and well-being, while physiological markers included creatine kinase, tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), and cortisol. Data were analyzed using 2-way repeated-measures ANOVA (p < 0.05). Both groups improved SJFT performance (p < 0.01), with no between-group differences. Block planning increased lower-limb peak power (p = 0.01; d = 0.90), whereas UP showed no meaningful change. Upper-limb power and CMJ did not change in either group. Internal load showed different temporal patterns between models. Block planning presented higher HRVcv values (p = 0.04), indicating greater autonomic perturbation. Creatine kinase and TNF-α increased over time in both groups (p ≤ 0.05), while cortisol showed an interaction without clear post hoc differences. In conclusion, BP improved lower-limb power but increased physiological strain, whereas UP elicited similar judo-specific improvements with lower recovery demands. These findings highlight the importance of training organization for balancing performance and recovery in elite judo athletes.

records.title: The effects of a 4-week protein overfeeding protocol on body composition and influence of FTO genotype in exercise-trained men and women.
records.publisher: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition

content.title: The effects of a 4-week protein overfeeding protocol on body composition and influence of FTO genotype in exercise-trained men and women.
content.abstract:
Background

High-protein diets have consistently been associated with favorable changes in body composition in both sedentary and exercise-trained populations. Despite abundant evidence supporting protein intakes above the recommended dietary allowance (RDA) for active individuals, the effects of deliberate protein overfeeding, particularly in those already consuming adequate protein, remain incompletely characterized. The primary purpose of this study was to examine the effects of a 4-week protein overfeeding protocol on body composition in exercise-trained men and women. The secondary purpose was to determine whether body composition adaptations differed by FTO rs9939609 genotype.

Methods

Fifty-six exercise-trained men and women (age: 22.40 ± 5.78 years; body mass: 75.47 ± 14.98 kg; BMI: 24.52 ± 3.50 kg/m2; resistance training: 5.12 ± 3.35 h/week) were enrolled in a 4-week dietary intervention. Participants were instructed to increase their daily protein intake by approximately 20% above baseline while maintaining habitual training. Body composition was assessed pre- and post-intervention using a multi-frequency bioelectrical impedance device (InBody® 270). Dietary intake was self-monitored via MyFitnessPal®. Thirty-five participants completed both pre- and post-testing assessments and constituted the primary analysis. Linear regression models adjusted for baseline values indicated that FTO genotype was not a significant predictor of body composition changes (p > 0.05).

Results

Protein intake trended toward a significant increase over the 4-week period (pre: 146 ± 66 g/day vs. post: 164 ± 79 g/day; p = 0.053), representing an approximate 12% increase. Total energy intake, carbohydrate, and fat intake did not significantly change. Lean body mass increased significantly (pre: 59.95 ± 14.14 kg vs. post: 60.62 ± 14.42 kg; p = 0.005; Cohen's d = 0.31) and total body water increased significantly (pre: 43.85 ± 10.35 L vs. post: 44.34 ± 10.55 L; p = 0.005). Fat mass (p = 0.424), body fat percentage (p = 0.149), and total body mass (p = 0.09) did not significantly change.

Conclusions

A 4-week modest protein overfeeding protocol in exercise-trained men and women was associated with a significant increase in lean body mass and total body water without concomitant increases in fat mass. These adaptations were not modified by FTO rs9939609 genotype. These findings support the contention that higher protein intakes do not promote fat accretion and may facilitate improvements in body composition in trained individuals.

records.title: Do Putative Human Reticulospinal Tract Properties Adapt Following Short-Term Isometric Resistance Training?
records.publisher: Medicine and science in sports and exercise

content.title: Do Putative Human Reticulospinal Tract Properties Adapt Following Short-Term Isometric Resistance Training?
content.abstract:
Purpose

The primary purpose of this study was to investigate whether isometric resistance training (RT) leads to reticulospinal tract (RST) adaptations.

Methods

A "RT group" of 30 healthy adults completed 4 weeks (15 sessions) of volume-matched unilateral elbow flexion RT involving high (32 repetitions/session at 70% maximal voluntary torque [MVT]) or low (64 repetitions/session at 35%MVT) loads. An additional 15 participants served as controls (CON group). Pre- and post-test MVT, RST properties (RST gain ratio derived from the StartReact assessment; startling auditory stimulus-conditioned/control motor evoked potential [MEP] ratio; and startling stimulus-conditioned/control cervicomedullary MEP [CMEP] ratio), CST excitability and intracortical inhibition properties (in response to transcranial magnetic stimulation) were assessed.

Results

MVT increased more in the RT group (+12.8%; n = 30) vs. CON group (-4.3%; n = 15; group (2) × time (2), p = 0.001). However, changes in RST properties assessed using a series of indirect measures did not differ between the RT group (-1.4% to 6.6%; n = 30) and CON group (-4.5% to 10.5%; n = 15; group (2) × time (2), 0.352 ≤ p ≤ 0.834).

Conclusions

RST adaptations within a sample of healthy young men and women, assessed using various indirect measurement approaches, did not occur following only 4 weeks of isometric elbow flexion RT. These findings add to the currently limited scientific evidence from short-term human RT intervention studies available to inform the use of RT for healthy individuals or patients primarily targeting the development of RST function.

records.title: Beyond the Hangover: Associations Between Binge Drinking, Health, and Performance in Young Adult Resistance-Trained Females.
records.publisher: Medicine and science in sports and exercise

content.title: Beyond the Hangover: Associations Between Binge Drinking, Health, and Performance in Young Adult Resistance-Trained Females.
content.abstract:
Purpose

The present study aimed to evaluate associations between resistance training and binge drinking in relation to musculoskeletal composition, physical fitness, cognitive function, and psychological wellness in young adult females.

Methods

Participants were categorized into four groups: sedentary low alcohol consumers (SL; n=12), sedentary binge drinkers (SB; n=12), resistance-trained low alcohol consumers (RTL; n=12), and resistance-trained binge drinkers (RTB; n=12). Measurements included body composition via DEXA scan, muscle quality via ultrasonography, and insulin sensitivity via oral glucose tolerance test. Physical performance was assessed using maximum chair stand power, vertical jump, broad jump, knee extensor torque, grip strength, and push-ups to failure. Tests and questionnaires were used to assess cognitive function and psychological wellness.

Results

Resistance-trained females had lower body fat than sedentary females (RTL = 29.28±4.27%; RTB = 29.03±3.67%; SL = 37.18±5.32%; SB = 34.83±3.54%; p<0.05), and RTL had more fat-free mass than SL and SB (RTL = 48.31±5.81 kg; SL = 38.08±6.59 kg; SB = 40.37±6.05 kg; both p<0.05). There were no differences between RTL and RTB in bone mineral density, muscle quality, or physical performance. RTL outperformed SL and SB on vertical jump (both p<0.05) while RTB outperformed SL and SB on broad jump. RTL had lower fasting blood glucose than RTB (88.92±12.09 mg/dL and 103.17 ± 10.21 mg/dL, respectively; p=0.008), and lower postprandial blood glucose than all groups (RTL = 103.83±19.82 mg/dL; RTB = 137.58±21.54 mg/dL; SL = 148.50±44.60 mg/dL; SB = 139.25±14.49 mg/dL; all p<0.05).

Conclusions

The results suggest that ≥1 year of binge drinking is associated with poorer metabolic health without differences in performance in young females. Further, frequent RT may mitigate the effects of binge drinking on body composition.

records.title: Exploratory serum renal biomarker and eGFR responses to high-protein diets during resistance versus concurrent training in resistance-trained men.
records.publisher: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition

content.title: Exploratory serum renal biomarker and eGFR responses to high-protein diets during resistance versus concurrent training in resistance-trained men.
content.abstract:
Background

High protein intake is common among resistance-trained athletes, but its association with renal biomarkers across different exercise modalities remains uncertain. This study investigated whether consuming a high-protein diet (3.2 g·kg⁻¹·d⁻¹) during 16 weeks of resistance training (RT) or concurrent training (CT) affects renal biomarkers and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) in resistance-trained men.

Methods

Forty-eight resistance-trained men (26 ± 6 years; BMI 25.6 ± 2.9 kg·m⁻²) were randomized to 16 weeks of RT or CT (4 sessions·wk⁻¹) while consuming either 1.6 or 3.2 g·kg⁻¹·d⁻¹ of protein in a 2 × 2 factorial design. Forty-four participants with complete pre- and post-intervention data were analyzed. Fasting blood samples were assessed for blood urea nitrogen (BUN), BUN/creatinine ratio, cystatin C, and eGFR calculated using the CKD-EPI creatinine (2021), cystatin C (2012), and creatinine-cystatin C (2021) equations. Within-group changes were evaluated using paired t-tests, and factorial effects were assessed using linear mixed-effects models (Time × Training × Protein).

Results

No statistically significant Time × Protein or Time × Training × Protein interactions were detected for any renal biomarker or eGFR estimate (all p ≥ 0.182). No significant within-group changes occurred in the 1.6 g·kg⁻¹·d⁻¹ groups (all p > 0.05). In both 3.2 g·kg⁻¹·d⁻¹ groups, BUN and cystatin C increased (all p ≤ 0.017), while eGFR estimates decreased (all p ≤ 0.009). The BUN/creatinine ratio remained unchanged (p ≥ 0.614). However, these within-group findings were descriptive because the corresponding interaction effects were not statistically significant.

Conclusions

In resistance-trained men, 16 weeks of high protein intake did not produce statistically detectable differences in renal biomarker or eGFR changes compared with moderate protein intake, irrespective of training modality. Although modest increases in BUN and cystatin C and small decreases in eGFR estimates were observed within the high-protein groups, these findings were not supported by significant factorial interactions. The limited sample size precludes excluding clinically meaningful differences, warranting further investigation in larger studies.

records.title: Independent and joint associations of physical activity, sedentary behavior, and sleep with vitamin D status in US adults: a cross-sectional NHANES study.
records.publisher: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition

content.title: Independent and joint associations of physical activity, sedentary behavior, and sleep with vitamin D status in US adults: a cross-sectional NHANES study.
content.abstract:
Background

Emerging evidence links movement behaviors to vitamin D status. This study investigated associations between physical activity (PA), sedentary behavior (SB), and sleep with vitamin D status and explored sex differences in these relationships.

Methods

This cross-sectional study included 3195 adults (49.1 ± 17.1 years, 45.5% males) from the 2021-2023 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey with complete data. Self-reported PA, SB, and sleep duration were assessed. Serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D was measured using high-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. Generalized linear and logistic regression models were performed.

Results

SB was negatively associated with vitamin D levels in the whole sample (β = -0.006; 95% confidence interval [CI]: -0.012, -0.001) and males (β = -0.008; 95% CI: -0.014, -0.002), but not females. Sleep duration was positively associated with vitamin D among males only (β = 0.023; 95% CI: 0.003, 0.043). Meeting both PA and SB guidelines showed the strongest and most consistent association with vitamin D sufficiency, observed across the whole sample (odds ratio [OR] = 2.129; 95% CI: 1.504, 3.012), males (OR = 2.013; 95% CI: 1.021, 3.967), and females (OR = 2.214; 95% CI: 1.360, 3.605).

Conclusions

Movement behaviors demonstrate independent and joint associations with vitamin D status in US adults, with modest sex-specific patterns that warrant replication. Combined adherence to PA and SB guidelines was consistently associated with greater odds of vitamin D sufficiency across sexes.

records.title: Lower-limb performance and muscle soreness after short-term dark chocolate intake in CrossFit®-trained women: an exploratory secondary analysis.
records.publisher: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition

content.title: Lower-limb performance and muscle soreness after short-term dark chocolate intake in CrossFit®-trained women: an exploratory secondary analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Dark chocolate (DC) has been proposed as a nutritional aid for exercise performance and recovery, but evidence in trained women remains limited. This exploratory secondary analysis examined selected lower-limb performance outcomes and delayed-onset muscle soreness (DOMS) in female CrossFit® athletes.

Methods

This secondary analysis included 15 trained female CrossFit® athletes from a randomized crossover trial. No separate a priori sample-size calculation was performed for these outcomes (minimum detectable paired effect, d_z = 0.78). DC (30 g/day, 85% cocoa), placebo chocolate (PLA), and an open-label control (CONN) were compared at four operationally defined menstrual-cycle assessments after three days of supplementation. DC-PLA allocation was blinded, but blinding success was not assessed. Outcomes were vertical jump height (VJH), knee isokinetic and isometric performance, and muscle-specific DOMS after the Cindy WOD.

Results

Condition effects survived FDR control for VJH and 19 of 22 dynamometry outcomes. Across assessments, VJH was 34.48 ± 5.09 cm with DC and 30.22 ± 2.34 cm with PLA (mean difference 4.27 cm, 95% CI 1.45 to 7.08; Holm-adjusted p = 0.017; g_av = 1.09). No condition-by-assessment interaction survived FDR control (all q ≥ 0.141). DOMS showed significant time effects for all three muscles, peaked at approximately 24 h, remained elevated at 48 h, and declined toward baseline by 72 h. A condition-by-time effect remained significant only for gastrocnemius soreness (Holm-adjusted p = 0.012; ηp2 = 0.212); no DOMS condition main effect or condition-by-assessment-by-time interaction was supported.

Conclusion

DC was associated with higher values for selected lower-limb outcomes, but these exploratory findings do not establish phase-specific efficacy, equivalent effects across cycle assessments, or a consistent DOMS benefit. Unusually large performance estimates and unmodeled period and carryover effects warrant caution.

records.title: Effects of milk fat globule membrane supplementation on physical function and body composition in older adults: a narrative review.
records.publisher: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition

content.title: Effects of milk fat globule membrane supplementation on physical function and body composition in older adults: a narrative review.
content.abstract:
Background

Healthy aging is a priority for many individuals; however, a decline in physical function and poor body composition are common age-related changes that can cause the added years from rising life expectancy to be spent in poor health. Consequently, understanding the mechanisms involved in aging has become increasingly important, including the role of phospholipids (PLs) and how age-related changes in PL content may interfere with lipid metabolism and normal functioning of the musculoskeletal system. Milk fat globule membrane (MFGM) is a bovine milk fraction rich in PLs that may have the potential to support good physical health, so that quality of life can rise alongside life expectancy.

Methods

This narrative review was based on a literature search conducted on Google Scholar, PubMed, and Scopus in May 2026 using the following keywords and Boolean operators: milk fat globule membrane OR MFGM AND physical function OR body composition OR older adults. Studies were included if they were randomized clinical trials (RCTs) investigating MFGM's effects on physical function and/or body composition in older adults.

Results

Findings suggest that MFGM supplementation, when consumed in conjunction with exercise, is an effective way to improve physical function in older adults, particularly among Japanese cohorts; however, changes in habitual diet in response to exercise, variable PL concentrations, and other added ingredients used in interventions may have influenced these results. In contrast, its effects on body composition appear more modest, with some studies reporting no benefits, especially when exercise was not part of the study design, or when compliance may have been a factor.

Conclusions

Beyond the combined use of supplementation and exercise, future RCTs should consistently report participant compliance and, where possible, examine MFGM as a standalone intervention to distinguish its effects from other bioactive ingredients. Greater standardization is also needed, particularly regarding PL dose. Studies should also aim to include participants from more diverse ethnic backgrounds to capture a wider range of physiological responses and improve generalizability of the findings.

records.title: Effects of extremely low-volume high-intensity interval training combined with iron supplementation versus iron supplementation alone on postural control in young women with iron deficiency anemia: a randomized controlled trial.
records.publisher: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition

content.title: Effects of extremely low-volume high-intensity interval training combined with iron supplementation versus iron supplementation alone on postural control in young women with iron deficiency anemia: a randomized controlled trial.
content.abstract:
Background

Recent research revealed postural control deterioration in young women with Iron Deficiency Anemia (IDA). To address this postural deficit, it is crucial to develop intervention strategies for postural rehabilitation in these individuals. This study aimed to explore the effect of 8-week extremely low-volume high-intensity interval training (HIIT) based on plyometric exercises combined with iron supplementation versus simple iron treatment on postural control of young women with IDA.

Methods

This randomized controlled trial enrolled young women with IDA aged 18-25 years, who were randomly assigned to a training group (TG; n = 16) or a non-training group (NTG; n = 17). All participants received oral iron supplementation (ferrous sulfate, 494.5 mg/day, administered as 247.25 mg twice daily), while the TG additionally completed an 8-week extremely low-volume HIIT program based on plyometric exercises. Hemoglobin (Hb) and serum ferritin concentrations were assessed, alongside muscle endurance, reaction time performance, and postural control. Muscle endurance was evaluated using the Killy test, reaction time performance using an online simple reaction time test, and postural control using a stabilometric platform under bipodal and semi-tandem stance conditions. Postural assessments were conducted with eyes open (EO) and eyes closed (EC) on firm and foam surfaces. All outcomes were measured at baseline and 72 h after the final intervention session.

Results

After the 8-week intervention, this study demonstrated significant improvements across both groups, irrespective of the intervention. However, TG showed significantly greater post-intervention improvements than NTG in Hb concentration (P = 0.042), muscle endurance (P < 0.001), and postural control. Superior postural control in TG was observed during a bipedal stance on a foam surface (EO: P = 0.001); EC: P = 0.035), as well as during semi-tandem stance on a firm surface (EO: P = 0.015; EC: P = 0.040) and on a foam surface (EO: P = 0.019; EC: P = 0.003), compared to the NTG. With a Bonferroni-adjusted significance threshold for multiple comparisons (α = 0.00625), between-group differences in postural control remained significant for bipedal foam EO (P = 0.001) and semi-tandem foam EC (P = 0.003).

Conclusions

The study showed that women with IDA improved their postural performance regardless of the intervention used.
